Alternatively, it is related (mutaʿallaq) to an omitted verb indicated by mawālī, and the estimate is "they inherit from what he leaves behind."

﴿والَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾ means "and those with whom your oaths have bound you." The word ʿaqadat (عَقَدَتْ) is the reading of the Kufan school, and the sentence means "your right hands have made a contract with them." This is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence) that has been given the meaning of a conditional, so its predicate (khabar) is ﴿فَآتُوهم نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ together with the fa' (فَ). The Kufan reading ʿaqadat (عَقَدَتْ) means "your oaths have bound their covenants." What is meant is the contract of alliance (ʿaqd al-muwālāh), which is lawful, and inheritance through it is established according to the majority of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, and this is our view. Its explanation: if a man or a woman embraces Islam and has no heir, and is neither Arab nor a freed slave, then he says to another, "wālaytuka" (والَيْتُكَ, "I have made an alliance with you") on the condition that you pay my blood-money (taʿqilanī, تَعْقِلَنِي) if I commit an offence, and that you inherit from me if I die. The other replies, "I accept." The contract is concluded, and the superior inherits from the inferior.

﴿إنَّ اللهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدًا﴾ means that He knows the unseen and the witnessed, and this is the most eloquent of promise and warning.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 34:**

﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ They take charge of them, commanding and forbidding, as rulers (al-wulat) take charge of their subjects (al-ra'aya). They are called qawwamun (protectors and maintainers) for this reason.

﴿Because Allah has made some of them excel others﴾ The pronoun in "ba'dihim" (some of them) refers to men and women. The meaning is: they have authority over women because of Allah's favouring some of them, namely the men, over some others, namely the women, in intellect, resolve, firmness, archery, strength, participation in raids, the complete fasting and prayer, prophethood, the caliphate, leadership of the prayer, the call to prayer (adhan), the sermon (khutba), congregational prayer, Friday prayer, the takbir of tashriq (the glorification of God recited on the days after the sacrifice) according to Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, testimony in the hudud (fixed penalties) and qisas (retaliation), the doubling of inheritance shares for men, their being the residuaries in inheritance, ownership of the marriage contract, divorce, and the attribution of lineage belongs to them, and they are the possessors of beards and turbans.

﴿And because they spend of their wealth﴾ This means: because their spending on women is from their own property. This indicates the obligation of maintenance (nafaqa) for wives upon the husband. Then he divided women into two types. The first type: ﴿So righteous women are obedient﴾, meaning obedient, carrying out what is incumbent upon them towards their husbands.

﴿Guarding in the absence [of their husbands]﴾ Guarding what is due in the absence (al-ghayb), which is the opposite of presence (al-shahada). That is, when the husbands are not present with them, they guard what they must guard in their absence: their chastity (furuj), the homes, and the property. It has also been said that "li-l-ghayb" means guarding their husbands' secrets.

﴿By what Allah has guarded﴾ By what Allah has guarded them when He enjoined husbands concerning them, saying: ﴿And live with them honourably﴾ [al-Nisa': 19]. Or it means: by what Allah has guarded them, protected them, and enabled them to guard the absent [husband's rights]. Or it means: by Allah's guarding of them, in that He has made them steadfast in this way.

The second type: ﴿And those from whom you fear disobedience﴾, that is, their disobedience and their haughtiness towards obeying their husbands. Nushuz (disobedience) literally means a raised place. From Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: it is that she belittles her husband's rights and does not obey his command.

﴿Then admonish them﴾ Warn them of the punishment of Allah, the Exalted, and of beating. Admonition (al-i'za) is speech that softens hard hearts and draws inclined to good the natures that turn away.

﴿And abandon them in the beds﴾ In the sleeping places, meaning: do not share covers with them. This is a metaphor for intercourse. Or it means that he turns his back to her in the bed, since he did not say "from the beds" (ʿan al-madaji').

﴿And beat them﴾ A beating that is not severe. He commanded admonition first, then abandonment in the beds, then beating, if admonition and abandonment do not succeed with them.

﴿If they obey you﴾ by giving up nushuz, ﴿then do not seek a way against them﴾, so remove from them any harassment. Here "sabilan" (a way) is the object (maf'ul) of "tabghu" (you seek), and it comes from baghaytu al-amr, meaning: I sought the matter.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Exalted and Great﴾ That is: if your hands are raised over them, know that His power over you is greater than your power over them, so avoid wronging them. Or: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Exalted and Great﴾ and you disobey Him despite His high station and the majesty of His dominion; then you repent and He accepts your repentance. Therefore you are more worthy of pardoning whoever wrongs you when he returns [to right conduct].

(p-356)

Then He addressed the rulers with His words: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two of them﴾. Its original form is "shiqaqan baynahuma" (a breach between them), and the word "shiqaq" was attributed to the adverbial noun "bayn" by way of extension (ittisa', the widening of usage), as in His words: ﴿Nay, it was the scheming of night and day﴾ [Saba': 32], whose original form is "bal makrun fi al-layli wa al-nahar" (nay, it was a scheming during the night and the day). "Shiqaq" means enmity and discord, because each of them does what is hard on the other, or inclines to a side (shiqq), meaning a direction other than the side of his companion. The pronoun refers to the spouses, although they have not been mentioned, because what indicates them has been mentioned, namely the men and the women.

﴿Then send an arbiter (hakam) from his people﴾: a man suited to judgment and to reconciling the two of them.

﴿and an arbiter from her people﴾. The sending of the two arbiters (hakamayn) from their respective families is because relatives know the inner circumstances better and are more eager for reconciliation, and the spouses feel more at ease with them, so they reveal what is in their hearts of love and hatred and of the desire for companionship or separation. The pronoun in ﴿if they intend reconciliation﴾ refers to the two arbiters, and the pronoun in ﴿God will bring about harmony between them﴾ refers to the spouses. That is: if they both intend to reconcile the matter between them, and their intention is sound, their mediation is blessed, and God, through the goodness of their effort, will bring about affection and agreement between the spouses and cast love and accord into their hearts. Alternatively, both pronouns refer to the arbiters, meaning: if they intend to reconcile the matter between them and to advise the spouses, God will bring about harmony between them, so they will agree upon one word and support one another in seeking agreement until the aim is achieved. Or both pronouns refer to the spouses, meaning: if they wish to reconcile what is between them and seek good, and for the breach to be removed from them, God will place affection between them, replacing discord with harmony and hatred with love. ﴿Indeed God is ever Knowing﴾ of the intention of the two arbiters, ﴿Aware﴾ of which of the spouses is the wrongdoer. They have no authority to separate the couple, contrary to the view of Malik, may God have mercy on him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 36:

﴿And worship Allah﴾. It has been said: servitude (ʿubūdiyya) is fourfold: fulfilling covenants, contentment with what exists, guarding the limits, and patience in the face of what is lost.

﴿And associate nothing with Him﴾: not an idol or anything else. It may also be read as a verbal noun, meaning: associating (ishrāk) in any form.

﴿And to parents, good treatment﴾: and treat them well, with good words, good deeds, and by spending on them when they are in need. (p-357)

﴿And to the near of kin﴾: and to everyone between whom and yourselves there is kinship, such as a brother, a paternal uncle, or others.

﴿And the orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is near﴾: the one whose neighbourhood is close, ﴿and the neighbour who is a stranger﴾: that is, the one whose neighbourhood is distant. Or, "the near neighbour" means the related one, and "the stranger neighbour" means the non-relative.

﴿And the companion by your side﴾: that is, the wife. From ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. Or it means the one who accompanies you by being at your side, whether as a fellow traveller, a partner in studying a branch of knowledge, or otherwise, or one sitting beside you in a gathering or a mosque.

﴿And the wayfarer﴾: the stranger, or the guest.

﴿And those whom your right hands possess﴾: the slaves, male and female.

﴿Indeed Allah does not love one who is arrogant﴾: proud, who disdains his relatives and neighbours and so does not turn towards them.

﴿Boastful﴾: who enumerates his virtues out of pride. For if he counts them as an acknowledgement (of Allah's bounty), he would be grateful (shakūr).

﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ ("those who are stingy") is in the accusative case as a *badal* (substitution, or apposition) for ﴿مَن كانَ مُخْتالا فَخُورًا﴾ ("whoever is self-deluded and boastful"). It is plural because it agrees with the meaning of *man* ("whoever"). Or it is accusative to express censure. Or it is nominative, as the *khabar* (predicate) of an omitted *mubtada'* (subject), whose implied meaning is: "They are ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ ("those who are stingy") ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ الناسَ بِالبُخْلِ﴾ ("and command people to be stingy"). Hamza and Ali read ﴿بِالبَخَلِ﴾ ("bakhal"), and they are two dialect forms, like *al-rushd* and *al-rashad* (both meaning "right guidance"). That is, they are stingy with what is in their own hands and with what is in the hands of others, and so they command others to be stingy with it, out of hatred for generosity. It has been said: *bukhl* (stinginess) is to eat oneself and not let others eat; *shuhh* (avarice) is to neither eat nor let others eat; *sakhā'* (generosity) is to eat and let others eat; and *jūd* (munificence) is to let others eat without eating oneself.

﴿وَيَكْتُمُونَ ما آتاهُمُ اللهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ ("and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty"): they hide the wealth and the ample circumstances with which Allah has blessed them. In a hadith: "When Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant." A governor of al-Rashid built a palace opposite his palace, and he was informed on about it. The man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, indeed the generous person is pleased to see the trace of his blessing, so I wished to please you by looking at the traces of your blessing," and his words pleased him. It has been said: it was revealed concerning the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابًا مُهِينًا﴾ ("and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment"), that is, they will be humiliated by it in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 38:

﴿Those who spend their wealth﴾ is conjoined to "those who are stingy" (alladhina yabkhaluna), or to "the disbelievers" (al-kafirun).

﴿Showing off to people﴾ is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose, i.e., an accusative of purpose), meaning: for boasting, and so that it may be said, "How generous they are!" – not seeking the countenance of Allah. They are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun), or the polytheists of Makkah.

﴿And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day. And whoever has Satan as a companion – how wretched a companion he is!﴾ – since he drives them to stinginess, showing off, and every evil. It is also permissible that this be a warning to them, that Satan will be joined with them in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 39:

﴿And what would it harm them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ What burden or harm would there be for them in believing and in spending in the way of Allah? The intended meaning is reproach and rebuke. Otherwise, there is every benefit and advantage in that, and this is like saying to the disobedient child: "What harm would it have done you to be dutiful?!" It is known that there is no harm in dutifulness, but it is a reproach and a rebuke. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾ is a warning (wa'id).

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] by an atom's weight﴾. It (*dharrah*, "atom") is: the small ant. It is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he put his hand into the dust, lifted it, then blew on it, and said: "Each one of these is a *dharrah*." It was also said: every particle of the floating dust seen in a ray of light coming through a window is a *dharrah*.

﴿And if it is a good deed﴾: and if the weight of the atom is a good deed. He made the pronoun of *mithqal* (weight) feminine only because it is annexed to a feminine noun. (*Ḥasanatan*) is the reading of the Ḥijāzī readers, with *kāna* used as a complete verb, and the *nūn* of *takun* was dropped for lightness because of its frequent use.

﴿He multiplies it﴾: He multiplies its reward. (*Yuḍaʿʿif-hā*) is the reading of the Meccan and Syrian readers.

﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾: and He gives its doer, from His own presence, a great reward. Since Allah has described it as great, who can know its measure, when He has also called the enjoyment of this world "little"?! This verse refutes the view of the Muʿtazilah (the rationalist school) on the eternal punishment of the one who commits a major sin, given that he also has many good deeds. [p. 359]

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 41:

﴿So how﴾ will these disbelievers among the Jews and others act ﴿when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ who will testify against them concerning what they did, and he is their prophet?

﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad,﴾

﴿against these people﴾, i.e., your community, ﴿as a witness﴾. "As a witness" is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), meaning: a witness over those who believed in belief, over those who disbelieved in disbelief, and over those who were hypocrites in hypocrisy. It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that: "He recited Surah al-Nisa to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he reached His saying: ﴿And We bring you against these people as a witness﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wept and said: 'Enough (ḥasbunā).'"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 42:

﴿Yawma'idhin﴾ is an adverbial complement (ẓarf) governed by His words: ﴿Those who disbelieved [in Allah] and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾: that they would be buried, so that the earth would be leveled over them as it is leveled over the dead. Or they will wish that they had not been resurrected, and that they and the earth were equal. Or the beasts will turn to dust, and they will wish for its condition. ﴿Tusawwā﴾ (تَسْوى) with a fatḥa on the tā', a light sīn, imāla, and the deletion of one of the two tā's of tatasawwā, is read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī. ﴿Tassawwā﴾ (تَسَّوّى), with the tā' assimilated into the sīn, is read by Madanī and Shāmī.

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾: this is a resumptive (mustaʾnaf) clause, meaning: and they will not be able to conceal it, because their limbs will bear witness against them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 43:

When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) prepared food and drink and invited a group of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), at a time when wine was still permitted, they ate and drank. Then they put one of them forward to lead them in the Maghrib prayer, and he recited: "Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, and you are not worshippers of what I worship" (Surah al-Kafirun), omitting the lām particles. Then there was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, meaning: do not approach it in this state, ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾, meaning: what you recite.

In this is evidence that the apostasy of a drunkard is not apostasy, for reciting Surah al-Kafirun with the lām particles dropped is disbelief. (p-360) Yet he was not judged to be a disbeliever until he was addressed by the name of faith. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not order that he be separated from his wife, nor that he renew his faith. Moreover, the community (ummah) has agreed that whoever utters a word of disbelief by his tongue in error is not judged a disbeliever.

﴿And not while impure﴾ is coordinated with ﴿while you are intoxicated﴾, because the position of the clause with the waw is the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl). It is as if it were said: do not approach prayer while intoxicated or impure. That is, do not pray while impure. The word junub (impure) applies to the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, because it is a noun that functions as a verbal noun, namely al-ijnāb (rendering oneself impure).

﴿Except as travellers passing through﴾ is a qualifier of the word "junuban" (impure). That is: do not approach prayer while impure, except as passers-through, that is, impure while resident, not while travelling. By "junub" is meant those who have not performed ghusl. It is as if it were said: do not approach prayer without having performed ghusl.

﴿Until you have washed (taghtasilū)﴾, that is: except that you be travellers unable to find water, performing tayammum. He referred to the one performing tayammum as a traveller, because the usual state of such a person is the absence of water. This is the position of Abū Ḥanīfa (may Allah have mercy on him), and it is also related from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: ﴿Do not approach prayer﴾ means the places of prayer, which are the mosques.

﴿And not while impure﴾, that is: do not approach the mosque while impure, ﴿except as travellers passing through﴾, that is, merely crossing through it. Thus it is permissible for the junub to pass through the mosque when there is need.

﴿And if you are sick, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the gha'it (low ground, used for relieving oneself), or you have touched women﴾: gha'it means the low, level ground, and they used to go there to relieve themselves, so it is used as a metaphor for minor impurity (ḥadath). ﴿Or you have touched women﴾ means you have had intercourse with them. This is related from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn ʿAbbās.

﴿And you find no water﴾ means you are unable to use it, either because it is absent, or distant, or because you lack the means of reaching it, or because of an obstacle such as a snake, a predator, or an enemy.

﴿Then perform tayammum﴾: the condition includes four categories: the sick, the travellers, those in a state of minor impurity, and those in a state of major impurity. The consequent, which is the command to perform tayammum, applies to all of them. So the sick, when they cannot find water due to weakness of movement and inability to reach it; the travellers, when they cannot find it due to its distance; and those in minor or major impurity, when they do not find it [due to some reason], may perform tayammum. (p-361) The verb "lamastum" (touched) is read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī.

﴿Clean earth (ṣaʿīd)﴾: al-Zajjāj said: it is the surface of the earth, whether dust or otherwise. Even if it is a rock with no dust upon it, if the one performing tayammum strikes his hand upon it and wipes, that is valid purification for him. The "min" in Surat al-Ma'idah is for the beginning of the limit (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), not for partitive meaning. ﴿Clean﴾ means pure. ﴿Then wipe your faces and hands﴾: it is said the bāʾ is redundant.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Pardoning (ʿAfuww)﴾ in granting dispensation and ease, ﴿Forgiving (Ghafūr)﴾ of error and shortcoming.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 44:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ — from the seeing of the heart (ru'yat al-qalb, mental perception). It is construed with ilā (to), and this is either in the sense of: "Has your knowledge not reached them?" or in the sense of: "Have you not looked at them?"

﴿Those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ — a share of knowledge of the Torah, and they are the rabbis (aḥbār) of the Jews.

﴿They purchase error﴾ — they exchange it for guidance (hudā), and this is remaining upon Judaism after the signs have become clear to them concerning the truthfulness of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that he is the Arab Prophet who was given good tidings of in the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿And they wish that you should go astray﴾ — you, O believers — ﴿from the way﴾, that is: the way of truth, just as they themselves went astray from it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 45:

﴿And Allah is most knowing﴾ of your enemies ﴿of your enemies﴾, and He has already informed you of the enmity of these people, so beware of them, and do not seek their counsel in your affairs.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector﴾ in benefit, ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a Helper﴾ in repelling harm. So trust in His guardianship and His support over them, or do not concern yourselves with them, for Allah will give you victory over them and suffice you against their plotting. "Waliyyan" (as a protector) and "naseeran" (as a helper) are in the accusative, either as tamyiz (specification) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 46:

﴿Among those who are Jews﴾ is an explanation of "those who were given a portion of the Book," or an explanation of "your enemies." What lies between them is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraḍ). Alternatively, it is connected to His words: ﴿a helper﴾, meaning: He will help you ﴿against those who are Jews﴾, like His words: ﴿And We helped him against the people who denied Our signs﴾ [al-Anbiya: 77]. Or it is connected to an omitted element, its estimate being: ﴿Among those who are Jews﴾ are a people ﴿who distort words﴾, so "a people" is the subject (mubtada'), "who distort" is its attribute (sifah), and the predicate (khabar) is ﴿among those who are Jews﴾, placed before it. The qualified noun, which is "a people," has been omitted, and its attribute has been put in its place. This is ﴿who distort words from their places﴾, meaning they turn them away from them and remove them. For when they change it and put in its place other words, they have turned it away from its places in the Torah, where God the Exalted placed it, and removed it from them. An example of this is their distortion of "ʾasmar rabʿah" (tawny, of medium build) from its place in the Torah by their putting "ʾadam ṭawīl" (dark, tall) in its place. Then he mentioned here ﴿from their places﴾, and in al-Ma'idah ﴿after their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41]. So the meaning of "from their places," according to what we have explained, is removing it from its places, in which God's wisdom required that it be placed, by what their desires demanded of substituting something else in its place. The meaning of ﴿after their places﴾ is that it had places which it was worthy to occupy; when they distorted it, they left it like a stranger who has no place after its places and its dwellings. The two meanings are close.

﴿And they say: "We hear"﴾ your word ﴿and "We disobey"﴾ your command. It was said: they said it in private. ﴿"And hear"﴾ our word ﴿"without being heard"﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the addressee, meaning: hear while you are not heard. It is a statement with two faces that admits of blame: meaning, hear from us, invoked against you, "May you not hear!" for if their supplication against him were answered he would hear nothing, and so he would be deaf, "not heard." They said this relying on the fact that their saying "May you not hear" is an answered supplication. Or: "hear" without being answered toward what you call to. Its meaning is: "not heard" with a reply that agrees with you, so it is as if you heard nothing. Or: "hear" while you are "not heard" a word you are pleased with, so your hearing turns away from it. It may also admit of praise, meaning: hear while you are "not heard" anything disliked, from the saying "Such-and-such made so-and-so hear" when he reviled him.

﴿And "Ra'ina"﴾ may mean "ra'ina": "let us address you," that is, "watch over us" and "wait for us." It may also be like a word in Hebrew or Syriac that they used to revile one another with, namely "ra'ina," so they made it a mockery of the religion and a derision of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), speaking to him with an ambiguous word, intending by it insult and humiliation, while showing by it reverence and honour.

﴿Twisting with their tongues﴾: twisting them and distorting them, meaning they twist the truth into falsehood with their tongues, where they put "ra'ina" in the place of "undhurna" and ﴿not heard﴾ in the place of "may you not hear something disliked." Or they twist with their tongues what they conceal of reviling into what they display of reverence, out of hypocrisy.

﴿And slander against the religion﴾ is their saying: "If he were truly a prophet, he would have been informed of what we believe about him." ﴿And if they had said: "We hear and we obey"﴾ and had not said "We disobey," ﴿and "Hear"﴾ and had not added to it ﴿"without being heard,"﴾ ﴿and "Look at us"﴾ instead of "ra'ina," ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ before God ﴿and more upright﴾, more just, and more sound.

﴿But God cursed them for their disbelief﴾: He drove them away and removed them far from His mercy because of their choosing disbelief.

﴿So they believe not, except a few﴾ of them, who did believe, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions; or, "except a little faith," weak and of no account, which is their belief in the One who created them alongside their disbelief in anyone else.

When they did not believe, this was revealed: ﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down﴾, meaning: the Qur'an.

﴿Confirming what is with you﴾, meaning: the Torah.

﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾, that is: We erase the outline of their features, the eyes, eyebrows, nose and mouth.

﴿And turn them back on their backs﴾, that is: We make them in the shape of their backs, which are the napes, with faces similarly effaced. The "fa'" (فاء) here indicates causation (lil-tasbib). If you take it to indicate sequence (lil-ta'qib), on the basis that they were threatened with two punishments, one following the other, then "turning them back after obliterating them" means: We obliterate faces and then turn the faces backward and the napes forward. It has also been said that the meaning of "obliteration" (tams) is transformation and alteration, as when He obliterated the wealth of the Copts and turned it into stones. By "faces" is meant their leaders and notables, so the meaning is: before the conditions of their notables are changed, when We strip them of their esteem and standing and clothe them in humiliation and retreat.

﴿Or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath﴾, that is: We will disgrace them by transforming them, as We transformed the companions of the Sabbath. The pronoun refers to "faces" if by that is meant the notables, or to "those who were given the Book" by way of iltifat (الالتفات, a shift in grammatical person or address). The threat was conditional on none of them believing, and some of them did believe, for Ibn Salam heard the verse while returning from Syria and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) as a Muslim before he went to his family, and said: "I did not think I would reach my family before Allah obliterates my face." Alternatively, Allah threatened them with one of two matters: the obliteration of faces or cursing them. If obliteration means the change in the conditions of their leaders, then one of the two has occurred; and if it means something else, then cursing has occurred, for they are cursed in every tongue. It has also been said that this is still awaited regarding the Jews.

﴿And the command of Allah was ever a thing done﴾, that is: the decreed matter, which is the punishment with which they were threatened, [is] certain to occur without doubt, so one of the two matters must occur if they do not believe.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ — if one dies upon it — ﴿but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. That is, what is less than shirk, even if it is a major sin (kabira), when there is no repentance (tawba). The summary: shirk is forgiven by means of repentance, and the promise of forgiveness for what is below it applies to one who has not repented. That is, He does not forgive the one who associates partners while he remains a associator, and He forgives the one who commits sin while he remains a sinner. The Prophet, may peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever meets Allah, the Exalted, not associating anything with Him, enters Paradise, and his sin does not harm him." Its restriction by His words ﴿for whom He wills﴾ does not take it out of its generality, as in His words: ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an dearer to me than this verse." The Mu'tazila's restriction of it to the one who repents is invalid, because disbelief (kufr) is forgiven by repentance, due to His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, what has already passed will be forgiven for them﴾ [al-Anfal: 38]. So what is below it is more deserving of being forgiven through repentance. The verse was brought for the purpose of explaining the distinction between them, and this is what we have mentioned. ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin﴾ — he lied a tremendous lie, and thereby deserved a painful punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 49:

It was revealed concerning those among the Jews and Christians who purified themselves (zakka nafsahu), when they said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones," and they said: "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians."

﴿Have you not seen those who purify themselves?﴾ It includes everyone who purifies himself, and He described it as the purification of deeds, the increase of obedience, and piety.

﴿Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ is an informing that the purification of Allah is the one that is taken into account, not the purification of anyone else, because He is the One who knows who is worthy of purification. Similar to it is: ﴿So do not justify yourselves; He knows best who is pious﴾ [al-Najm: 32]. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ meaning: those who purify themselves will be punished for their self-purification to the full extent of their recompense, or whomever He wills will be rewarded for their purity, and nothing will be reduced from their reward ﴿a fatil﴾, the measure of a fatil, which is what forms from twisting the fingers, from the dirt.

(p-365)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 50:

﴿Look how they invent lies against God.﴾ In their claim that they are pure before God. ﴿And that is sufficient as a manifest sin﴾ by their claim this, among all their other sins.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 51:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ He means: the Jews.

﴿They believe in al-Jibt (idols and sorcery)﴾ That is, the idols, and everything they worshipped besides Allah.

﴿And al-Taghut (the transgressor)﴾ Satan.

﴿And they say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe, as to the way."﴾ The reason for this is that Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, two Jews, went out to Makkah with a group of Jews, seeking alliance with Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "You are the People of the Book, and you are closer to Muhammad than we are, and he is closer to you than to us. So we do not feel safe from your deception. Prostrate to our gods until we are reassured about you." And they did so. This is their belief in al-Jibt and al-Taghut, because they prostrated to the idols and obeyed Iblis, may the curse of Allah be upon him, in what they did. Then Abu Sufyan said: "Are we better guided in the way, or is Muhammad?" Ka'b said: "You are better guided in the way."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 52:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾, and He has removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper﴾, meaning, one whose help is taken into account.

Then he described the Jews with stinginess and envy, and these are among the worst of traits. They withhold what is theirs and wish for what belongs to others. So He said: ﴿Or do they have a share of the kingdom?﴾ Here "am" (or) is disjunctive (munqati'ah), and the meaning of the hamza is denial: that they should have a share of the kingdom.

﴿Then they would not give the people even a naqir﴾ That is: if they had a share of the kingdom—that is, the kingdom of the people of this world, or the kingdom of Allah—then they would not give anyone even the quantity of a naqir, due to their extreme stinginess. The naqir is the small pit on the back of a date-stone, and it is a proverbial expression for a very small amount, like the fatil (the thread in the cleft of a date-stone).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 54:

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ Rather, do they envy the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, for denying envy and considering it reprehensible? They were envying them for what Allah had given them of victory, dominance, the increase of honour, and advancement every day.

﴿We had indeed given the family of Abraham the Book﴾ i.e., the Torah.

﴿and wisdom﴾ i.e., admonition and understanding (fiqh).

﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾ meaning: the kingdom of Joseph, David, and Solomon, peace be upon them. Here is an argument against them based on what they know of Allah giving the Book and wisdom to the family of Abraham, who are the forefathers of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that it is not novel for Allah to give him the like of what His forefathers were given.

﷿ "Among them is the one who believed in it" — among the Jews there were those who believed in what was mentioned of the story of the family of Abraham, "and among them is the one who turned away from it" — who denied it while knowing it to be true; or, among the Jews there were those who believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among them were those who denied his prophethood and turned away from him. "And Hell suffices as a blazing fire" for those who turn away.

Note on rendering: the Arabic text reads "فَمِنهم مَن آمَنَ بِهِ" and "وَمِنهم مَن صَدَّ عَنْهُ," which the translation above renders with the Qur'anic meaning inside quotation marks. The verse is ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ صَدَّ عَنْهُ وَكَفَى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا﴾.

Corrections to the above: the honorific rendering should follow the instruction, so the opening should read as follows.

**Corrected translation:**

Among them is the one who believed in it: among the Jews were those who believed in what was mentioned of the story of the family of Abraham. "And among them is the one who turned away from it": who denied it while knowing it to be true. Or, among the Jews were those who believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and among them were those who denied his prophethood and turned away from him. "And Hell suffices as a blazing fire" for those who turn away.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs – We will surely cause them to enter⁠ Fire﴾ — we will make them enter — ﴿Fire. Every time their skins are roasted﴾ — burned — ﴿We will replace them with other skins﴾ — We will return those skins not burning. So the substitution (al-tabdil) and change (al-taghyir) are due to the difference of the two states (al-hay'atayn), not the difference of the two origins (al-aslayn) according to the People of Truth (Ahl al-Haqq), contrary to the Karramiyya. And from Fudayl: he makes the ripe [skin] not ripe.

﴿That they may taste the punishment﴾ — that its tasting may continue for them and not cease, like your saying to one who is mighty: "May God make you mighty" — i.e., may He keep you in your might.

﴿Indeed, God is ever Mighty﴾ — dominant in retribution; nothing He wills against the criminals is prevented from Him.

﴿Wise﴾ — in what He does with the disbelievers.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are spouses purified﴾ from impurities, menstruation, and postnatal bleeding.

﴿And We shall admit them into a shade, extended and dense﴾. The phrase ﴿ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا﴾ is an attributive form derived from the word for shade (ظِل, _ẓill_) to emphasize its meaning, as one says ﻟَيْلٌ ألْيَلُ (_laylun alyal_, "a night of utter darkness"). It is that which is long and lush (_faynān_), with no gaps (_jawb_) in it; and constant, which the sun does not erase (_lā tansakhuhu al-shams_); and temperate (_sajsaj_), with neither heat nor cold in it. There is nothing like this except the shade of Paradise. (p-٣٦٧)

Then He addressed the rulers, commanding them to render the trusts and to judge with justice, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. It has also been said: the duty of rendering trusts includes the performance of the obligations (fara'id), which are the trust of Allah Most High that man has borne, and the guarding of the senses (al-hawass), which are the deposits of Allah Most High.

﴿And when you judge between the people﴾, i.e., when you pass judgment, ﴿to judge with justice﴾, i.e., with equity and fairness. It has also been said: "Indeed, Uthman ibn Talhah ibn Abd al-Dar was the keeper (sadin) of the Ka'bah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken the key of the Ka'bah from him. When the verse was revealed, he commanded Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, to return it to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah has revealed a Qur'an concerning your matter,' and he recited the verse to him. So Uthman embraced Islam, and Jibril, peace be upon him, descended and informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the custodianship (al-sadanah) would remain in the descendants of Uthman forever."

﴿Indeed, how excellent is what Allah admonishes you with﴾. "Ma" is an indefinite noun in the accusative, described by "yaizukum bihi" (admonishes you with it), as if it were said: "an excellent thing with which He admonishes you." Or it is a relative pronoun in the nominative position, its relative clause being what follows it, i.e., "how excellent is the thing with which He admonishes you." The item praised is omitted, i.e., "how excellent is that with which He admonishes you," namely the command to render trusts and to be just in judgment. The reading with a kasrah on the nun and sukun on the 'ayn is that of Madani and Abu 'Amr. The reading with a fathah on the nun and kasrah on the 'ayn is that of Shami, Hamzah, and Ali.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Seeing﴾ of your deeds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 59:

When He commanded the rulers to render the trusts and to judge with justice, He commanded the people to obey them, by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾. That is, the rulers (ulat), or the scholars (ulama'), because their command is executed over the commanders (al-umara').

﴿And if you dispute over anything﴾, that is, if you and those in authority differ over any matter of the religion, ﴿then refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾. That is, (p-368) return to the Book and the Sunnah concerning it.

﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. That is, faith necessitates obedience and not disobedience. The verse indicates that obedience to the commanders is obligatory when they agree with the truth; but when they oppose it, there is no obedience to them, due to His ﷺ saying: "There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." It is related that Maslamah ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan said to Abu Hazim: "Were we not commanded to obey you, by His saying: ﴿and those in authority among you﴾?" Abu Hazim said: "Has not obedience been removed from you when you oppose the truth, by His saying: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, then refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾?" That is, the Qur'an and the Messenger during his lifetime, and to his hadiths after his death.

﴿That﴾ is a reference to the referral, that is, the referral to the Book and the Sunnah.

﴿Better﴾ in the immediate sense, ﴿and better in outcome (ta'wil)﴾ in the final consequence.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 60:

There was a dispute between Bishr, a hypocrite (munafiq), and a Jew. The Jew invited him to the Prophet ﷺ, knowing that he would not accept bribes, while the hypocrite invited him to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf so that he could bribe him. They brought their case to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ruled in favour of the Jew, but the hypocrite was not satisfied and said: "Come, let us take our dispute to 'Umar." The Jew said to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has ruled in my favour, but he was not content with his judgment." 'Umar said to the hypocrite: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes." 'Umar said: "Stay where you are until I come out to you." 'Umar went in, took his sword, then came out and struck the hypocrite's neck with it, saying: "This is how I judge for whoever is not content with the judgment of Allah and His Messenger." Then there was revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim﴾ and Jibril, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed 'Umar has distinguished between truth and falsehood." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "You are al-Faruq."

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, desiring﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in ﴿claim﴾. ﴿to seek judgment to the Taghut﴾, i.e., Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Allah named him "Taghut" because of his extreme transgression (tughyan) and hostility toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Or it is by way of comparison with Satan. Or the choice of seeking judgment from other than Allah over seeking judgment from Him is made into seeking judgment from Satan, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And they were commanded to reject it, and Satan desires to lead them astray﴾ from the truth ﴿into far error﴾, persistent until death.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 61:

﴿And when it is said to them﴾ (to the hypocrites), ﴿"Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger"﴾ (for judgment), ﴿you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion﴾ (they turn away from you towards someone other than you, so that they may bribe him, and he would then judge in their favour).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 62:

﴿Then how﴾ will their condition be, and how will they act? ﴿When a disaster strikes them﴾ because of the killing of Umar of Bishr, ﴿for what their hands have sent ahead﴾ of going to judgment before someone other than you, and of their accusing you of being unjust in your ruling.

﴿Then they come to you﴾ i.e., the companions of the slain man from among the hypocrites,

﴿swearing by Allah﴾ (this is a circumstantial clause, ḥāl) ﴿"We intended nothing but﴾ good ﴿and reconciliation"﴾ in what we intended by going to judgment before someone other than you.

﴿Nothing but good﴾, not harm, ﴿and reconciliation﴾ between the two disputants. We did not intend to oppose you or to be displeased with your ruling. This is a warning to them for their action, and that they will regret it at a time when regret will not benefit them and excuses will not avail them. It was also said: the guardians of the hypocrite came seeking blood-money for him, though Allah had nullified his claim, and they said: "We intended by going to judgment before Umar only that he would show kindness to our companion through a just ruling and by reconciling him with his opponent, and it never occurred to us that he would rule in his favour according to what he ruled."

**Surah 4, verse 63:**

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾ of hypocrisy, ﴿so turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word.﴾ Turn away from accepting their excuses; admonish them with rebuke and disapproval, and exert yourself in admonishing them with intimidation and warning. Or, turn away from punishing them, admonish them in reproach, and convey the full extent of the admonition that is in your inner self regarding their misdeeds. Eloquence (al-balaghah) is that one conveys with his tongue the full extent of what is in his heart. The phrase ﴿in their souls﴾ is connected to ﴿speak to them﴾, meaning: speak to them concerning their wicked souls and their hearts folded upon (p-370) hypocrisy, ﴿a far-reaching word﴾ that reaches them and makes an impression upon them.

﴿And We did not send any messenger﴾, i.e., never a messenger.

﴿to be obeyed by God's permission﴾: by His granting them success in obeying him and facilitating it, or because of God's permission to obey him, and because He commanded those to whom he was sent to obey him, since he conveys (mu'addi) from God. So his obedience is the obedience of God. ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed God﴾. ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves﴾, by seeking judgment from the tāghūt (false object of worship or tyrant), ﴿came to you﴾ repentant of hypocrisy (nifāq), apologizing for what they had committed of dissension (shiqāq),

﴿and asked God for forgiveness﴾ for hypocrisy and dissension, ﴿and the Messenger asked forgiveness for them﴾ by intercession on their behalf. The governing element (al-'āmil) of ﴿when they had wronged themselves﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of inna (the particle of emphasis), which is ﴿came to you﴾. The meaning is: if their coming had occurred at the time of their wronging, together with their seeking forgiveness and the Messenger's seeking forgiveness for them.

﴿they would have found God Relenting, Merciful﴾: they would have known Him as one who relents (tawwāb), i.e., He would have turned to them in mercy. He did not say "you asked forgiveness for them," but shifted to the mode of iltifāt (a shift in grammatical person), exalting his status (ﷺ) and magnifying his seeking of forgiveness, and alerting that the intercession of one whose name is "the Messenger" has a high station with God.

﴿Most Merciful﴾ toward them. It is said: a Bedouin came after his burial (ﷺ), threw himself upon his grave, and poured some of its dust over his head, saying: "O Messenger of God, you spoke and we heard you, and among what was revealed to you was ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves﴾" to the end of the verse. "I have wronged myself, and I have come to you seeking God's forgiveness for my sin. So seek forgiveness for me from my Lord." Then he was called from his grave: "You have already been forgiven!"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 65:

﴿So by your Lord﴾: i.e., "fa-wa-Rabbika" (by your Lord), like His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them﴾ [al-Hijr: 92]. The "lā" is extra (ma-zīdah), for emphasizing the meaning of the oath. The answer to the oath is ﴿they do not believe﴾. Or the estimate is: "fa-lā" means "the matter is not as they say." Then He said: ﴿and by your Lord, they do not believe﴾ ﴿until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾, i.e., in what has become confused and mixed up among them. From this comes the word "shajar" (tree), due to the interlacing of its branches.

﴿Then they find within themselves no discomfort﴾ (ḥaraj), i.e., constriction ﴿concerning what you have decided﴾. I.e., their hearts are not constricted by your ruling. Or [it means] doubt, because the doubter is in constriction about his matter (p-371) until certainty appears to him. ﴿And they submit with full submission﴾, and yield to your judgment with full yielding. Its true meaning: he gave himself over to him and surrendered it, i.e., made it sound (sālimah) for him, i.e., pure. "Taslīman" is an emphatic verbal noun (maṣdar) for the verb, in the position of repeating it, as if it were said: "and they yield to your ruling with a yielding that has no doubt in it, outwardly or inwardly." The meaning: they do not become believers until they are pleased with your ruling and your judgment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 66:

﴿And if We had prescribed for them﴾ — upon the hypocrites; i.e., if Our prescribing had been applied to them.

﴿That kill yourselves﴾ — here "an" (أنِ) is the explanatory particle (al-mufassirah). ﴿Kill yourselves﴾ means: expose yourselves to being killed through jihad. Or: even if We had obligated upon them the like of what We obligated upon the Children of Israel, namely killing themselves,

﴿or leave your homes﴾ — through emigration (hijrah) — ﴿they would not have done it﴾ — because of their hypocrisy. The pronoun "hu" (الهاءُ) refers to one of the two verbal nouns (masdar) of the two verbs, namely the killing or the leaving; or it refers to what was prescribed, since "kataba 'alayhi" indicates it.

﴿except a few of them﴾ — (qalilan) is the reading of Ibn 'Amir (Shami), in the accusative as an exception; the nominative is as a substitute (badal) for the waw of "fa'aluhu" (they did it).

﴿And if they had done what they were being admonished with﴾ — following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and submitting to his ruling.

﴿it would have been better for them﴾ — in both abodes — ﴿and firmer in establishing them﴾ — in their faith, and further from wavering in it.

﴿And then﴾ is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "And what will they have after being made steadfast?" So it was said: "And then," even if they had remained steadfast, ﴿We would surely give them from Us a great reward﴾, meaning abundant reward that does not end.

Qur'an 4:68 (commentary on the verse): "And We would have guided them to a straight path."

"Guided them" (wa-la-hadaynahum): the second object (maf'ul thani) of this verb is "a path" (sirat), and "straight" (mustaqiman) is its description. That is, We would have made them steadfast upon the true religion.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 69:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – then those are with those whom Allah has blessed: of the prophets, the truthful (al-siddiqin), and the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ like the most excellent companions of the prophets. The siddiq (one who is truthful, a term for a person of exceptional sincerity): one who exceeds in the truthfulness of his outward conduct in dealings, and of his inward state through vigilance (al-muraqaba), or the one whose speech is confirmed by his action.

﴿And the martyrs﴾ those who were killed (ustushhidu) (p-372) in the way of Allah. ﴿And the righteous﴾ those whose circumstances are good and whose deeds are excellent.

﴿And excellent is those as companions﴾ meaning: how excellent are those as companions! It is like the word ṣadīq (friend) and khalīṭ (close associate) in that the singular and the plural are equal in it.

Ḏālika (ذَلِكَ) is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is "al-faḍlu mina-llāh" (ﷻ) — the grace is from God. Or, al-faḍlu is its attribute (ṣifa), and "min Allāh" is the predicate.

The meaning: what the obedient are given of great reward and of companionship with those upon whom God has bestowed favour is from God, because He has graciously bestowed it upon them. Or he intends: the excellence of those upon whom favour is bestowed and their rank is from God. ﴿And sufficient is God as Knower﴾ of His servants, and of who deserves the grace. The verse indicates that whatever God does to His servants is grace from Him, unlike what the Mu'tazilah say.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 71:

﴿O you who believe, take your precaution⁠﴾ Al-hidhr (ﺣِﺬْر) and al-hadhar (ﺣَﺬَر) have the same meaning, namely guarding against harm. They are like al-ithr and al-athar (the two forms of "trace"). It is said: "He took his precaution" (akhadha hidhrahu), when he became alert and guarded himself against what is feared. It is as if he made caution (al-hadhar) his instrument by which he protects himself and by which he safeguards his soul. The meaning is: be cautious and guard yourselves against the enemy.

﴿Then go forth in separate groups⁠﴾ Go out to the enemy in scattered groups, one expedition after another. Thus al-thubat (ثُبات) means groups, whose singular is thubah (ثُبَة).

﴿Or go forth all together⁠﴾ That is, gathered together, or with the Prophet (ﷺ), because gathering without a leader is not complete, and a necklace without a thread (al-wasita, the connecting element) cannot be strung together. Or [the meaning is]: ﴿Then go forth in groups⁠﴾ if the mobilization is not general, and ﴿or go forth all together⁠﴾ if the mobilization is general. Here "thubat" (ثُباتٍ) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and likewise "jamī'an" (جَمِيعًا).

The letter lam in ﴿And indeed among you is one who﴾ is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'), with the same function it has in ﴿indeed Allah is Most Forgiving﴾, and "man" (who) is a relative pronoun. ﴿Would certainly delay﴾: the lam is the answer to an omitted oath, its underlying sense being: "And indeed among you is one who—I swear by Allah—would certainly delay." The oath and its answer form the relative clause (silah) of "man," and the pronoun returning from it to "man" is the one concealed within "would certainly delay." The meaning is: would certainly lag behind (layatharaqqalanna), and would stay back from jihad. Baṭua (to be slow) has the same meaning as abta'a (to delay, to be late). One says mā baṭu'a bika, using the preposition bi- (with). The address is to the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His words "among you" mean outwardly, not inwardly, referring to the hypocrites, who say: "Why do you kill yourselves? Be patient until the matter becomes clear."

﴿If a calamity befalls you﴾, namely a killing or a defeat, (p-373) the one who delays "says": ﴿Allah has certainly blessed me in that I was not present with them as a witness﴾, that is, present, so that I would be struck by what struck them.

**﴿And if there befalls you a bounty from Allah﴾**: a conquest or spoils.

**﴿He will surely say﴾**: this laggard, distressed over what of the spoils he missed, not seeking reward. **"كَأنْ" (ka'anna, "as if")** is the lightened form of the heavy (ka'anna, with emphatic noun) and its noun is omitted, meaning "as if he [were]." **"لَمْ يَكُنْ" (lam yakun)** with the ya' is the reading of Makki and Hafs.

**﴿between you and him there was [no] affection﴾**: this is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD) between the verb, which is "لَيَقُولَنَّ" (layaqulanna, "he will surely say"), and its object, which is **﴿Would that I had been with them!﴾**. The meaning is: as if there had never been any prior affection between him and you, because the hypocrites used to show affection to the believers outwardly, even though inwardly they plotted harm against them.

**"فَأفُوزَ" (fa-afuza, "that I would triumph")** is in the accusative because it is the answer to the wish (tamanni). **﴿a great triumph﴾**: that I would take a generous share of the spoils.

﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell﴾ يَبِيعُونَ (sell) ﴿the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾. The intended meaning is the believers who prefer the deferred life over the immediate one and exchange the one for the other. That is, if those whose hearts are diseased and whose intentions are weak hold back from fighting, then let the steadfast and sincere fight. Alternatively, يَشْرُونَ (yashrūna) means "buy," and the intended meaning is the hypocrites who buy the life of this world with the Hereafter. They were admonished to change the hypocrisy within them, to make their faith in Allah and His Messenger sincere, and to strive in the way of Allah with the striving due to Him.

﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward.﴾ Allah promised the one who fights in the way of Allah, whether he is victorious or is granted victory, a great reward in return for his effort in exalting the religion of Allah.

(p-374)

"What is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah"—[this is] a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar). This interrogative, in negation, serves as a reproach for delay, and in affirmation, as a denunciation.

﴿لا تُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللهِ﴾ ("you do not fight in the way of Allah") is a circumstantial clause (hal), and the element governing it is the stability (al-istiqrar) [implied in the sentence], just as you say: "What is the matter with you, standing?" The meaning is: "And what reason do you have for abandoning fighting, when its motives have become manifest?!"

﴿والمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ ("and the oppressed") is in the genitive by conjunction (ma'tuf) upon "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah), meaning: in the way of Allah and in the deliverance of the oppressed. Or it is in the accusative as a specification (ikhtisas) from it, meaning: and the deliverance of the oppressed is specified from the way of Allah, because the way of Allah is general to every good, and the deliverance of the oppressed Muslims from the hands of the disbelievers is among the greatest of goods and the most specific of them. The oppressed (al-mustad'afun) are those who embraced Islam in Makkah, and the polytheists prevented them from emigrating, so they remained among them, humiliated and oppressed, suffering severe harm from them ﴿from the men and the women and the children﴾. He mentioned the children to record the extremity of their wrongdoing, since their harm reached even children who were not legally responsible, to humble their fathers and mothers. Also, the oppressed used to include their children in their supplications, seeking the descent of Allah's mercy through the supplication of their young ones who had committed no sin, as the people of Yunus (peace be upon him) did. From Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "I and my mother were among the oppressed, from the women and the children."

﴿الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أخْرِجْنا مِن هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ﴾ ("those who say: Our Lord, bring us out from this town") means: Makkah.

﴿الظالِمِ أهْلُها﴾ ("whose people are wrongdoers") — "al-zalim" is an adjective of "al-qaryah" (the town), except that it is attributed to its people (ahluha), so it takes the grammatical case of "al-qaryah" because it is its attribute, and it is masculine because of its attribution to "al-ahl" (the people), as you say: "from this town whose people have done wrong."

﴿واجْعَلْ لَنا مِن لَدُنْكَ ولِيًّا﴾ ("and appoint for us from Yourself a protector") who will manage our affairs and rescue us from our enemies,

﴿واجْعَلْ لَنا مِن لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا﴾ ("and appoint for us from Yourself a helper") who will give us victory over them. They were calling upon Allah for deliverance and seeking His help, so the emigration to Madinah was made easy for some of them, and some remained until the Conquest. Then Allah appointed for them from Himself the best of protectors and helpers, namely Muhammad (ﷺ), so he managed their affairs in the best manner and gave them the most powerful victory (p-375). When Muhammad (ﷺ) went out, he appointed 'Attab ibn Usayd, and they saw from him the guardianship and support they had wished for. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "He used to support the weak against the strong, until they became more honored by him than the oppressors."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 76:

God encouraged the believers by [informing them] that they fight in the way of God (sabil Allah), so He is their Ally (waliyy) and Helper (nasir), whereas their enemies fight in the way of Satan (al-Shaytan), so they have no ally except Satan. ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of the Taghut﴾ — i.e., Satan — by His saying: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾ — i.e., the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan﴾ — i.e., his whisperings. It is said: al-kayd (plotting, scheming) is striving to corrupt a situation through deception. ﴿Is ever weak﴾ because it is delusion (ghurur) that does not lead to any real outcome; or, his plotting, compared with the help of God, is weak.

The Muslims were restrained from fighting the disbelievers as long as they were in Makkah, and they wished that permission would be given to them to do so. Then there was revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"﴾, that is, from fighting,

﴿and establish the prayer and give the zakah. But when fighting was prescribed for them﴾, that is, obligated in Madinah, ﴿behold, a party of them fear men as they fear Allah﴾, fearing that the disbelievers would fight them, just as they fear that Allah will send down His punishment upon them. This is not doubt about the religion, nor aversion to it, but rather recoil from risking their lives and fear of death. Shaykh Abu Mansur, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This is a fear of natural disposition, not that they, in belief, disliked the judgment and command of Allah. A person is naturally inclined to dislike what generally carries the fear of his destruction. "as they fear Allah" (ka-khashyati Allah) is an idafah of the verbal noun to its object, and its position is accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "yakhshawna" (they fear). That is: they fear people like (mithl) the fear of Allah, that is, resembling the people of the fear of Allah. ﴿Or even greater in fear﴾ is conjoined to the circumstantial clause, that is: or even greater in fear than the people of the fear of Allah. And "aw" (or) here indicates choice (li-l-takhyir), meaning: if you say "their fear of people is like the fear of Allah," you are correct, and if you say "it is greater," you are also correct, because they experienced something like it and more.

﴿And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ That is: why did You not give us respite until death, so that we would die on our beds? This is a question seeking the wisdom behind the prescription of fighting for them, not an objection to His judgment, as evidenced by the fact that they were not rebuked for this question; rather, they were answered with His saying: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah."﴾ The enjoyment of this world is little and transient, while the enjoyment of the Hereafter is abundant and lasting; and what is abundant, when it is on the verge of ceasing, is little, so how about what is little and transient?! ﴿And you will not be wronged the amount of a thread﴾, that is, you will not be deprived of the least of your rewards for the hardships of fighting, so do not be averse to it. The reading with the ya' (yuẓlamūna, "they will not be wronged") is that of Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and ʿAlī.

Then He informed that caution does not save one from decree, by His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you﴾. "Ma" is superfluous, serving to emphasize the conditional meaning in "ayna" (wherever). ﴿Even if you were in towers﴾ fortresses or palaces ﴿well-built﴾ lofty.

﴿And if good befalls them﴾ a blessing of abundance and ease, ﴿they say, "This is from Allah."﴾ They attributed it to Allah. ﴿And if evil befalls them﴾ an affliction of drought and hardship, ﴿they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]."﴾ They ascribed it to him, saying: "This is from you, and it was only because of your ill omen." That was because the hypocrites and the Jews, whenever good befell them, would praise Allah, the Exalted, and whenever something disliked befell them, they would attribute it to Muhammad (ﷺ). So Allah, the Exalted, refuted them by His saying: ﴿Each is from Allah﴾, and the noun to which it is added is omitted, meaning: all of that [is from Allah], for He extends provision and restricts it.

﴿So what is with these people that they hardly understand﴾ comprehend ﴿any statement﴾, so that they would know that Allah is the One who extends and restricts, and that all of that proceeds from wisdom.

Then He said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you﴾ — O human being, a general address. Al-Zajjaj said: the one addressed is the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is others. ﴿Good﴾ means blessing and kindness.

﴿Then it is from Allah﴾ out of His bounty and favour.

﴿And whatever evil befalls you﴾ — of calamity and misfortune — ﴿it is from yourself﴾, that is, from your own doing: ﴿it is because of what your hands have earned﴾,

﴿And whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾. ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger﴾ — not as one whose decree is fixed, to the point that they attributed hardship to you. Or: We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, so conveying the message is incumbent upon you, and good and evil are not incumbent upon you.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ that you are His messenger. It is said that this is connected to the first part, meaning: ﴿they hardly understand any speech﴾, saying, "Whatever has befallen you." The Mu'tazilites' interpreting "good" and "evil" in this verse as obedience and disobedience is clear distortion, and the phrase "whatever has befallen you" calls out against it, since with actions one says, "what you have struck" (ma aṣabta). Moreover, they do not say that good deeds are from Allah by way of creation and origination, so how could they have any proof in this? "Shahidan" is a specification (tamyiz).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 80:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah﴾ Because he does not command or forbid except in accordance with what Allah has commanded and forbidden. So his obedience in his commands and prohibitions is obedience to Allah. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ from obedience, and turns his back on it, ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾ to keep watch over their deeds, to hold them accountable for them, and to punish them.

And ﴿they say﴾: the hypocrites say, "When you order them to something, it is ﴿obedience﴾." Here ﴿طاعَةٌ﴾ (ṭā'ah, obedience) is the *khabar* (predicate) of an omitted *mubtada'* (subject), meaning: "Our matter and our affair is obedience."

﴿And when they go forth﴾ (fa-idhā barazū), meaning they went out, ﴿from your presence, a group of them plotted﴾ (bayyata ṭā'ifatun minhum), meaning they contrived and arranged. It may be derived from *al-baytūtah* (spending the night), because devising and arranging a matter is done at night, or from *abyāt al-shi'r* (lines of poetry), because the poet turns them over and arranges them. ﴿بَيَّتَ﴾ is read with *idghām* (assimilation) by Ḥamzah and Abū 'Amr.

﴿Other than what you say﴾ (ghayra alladhī taqūl): contrary to what you said and ordered, or contrary to what they themselves said and pledged of obedience, because they concealed rejection, not acceptance, and disobedience, not obedience. They are hypocrites only in what they say and show outwardly.

﴿And Allah records what they plot﴾ (wallāhu yaktubu mā yubayyitūn): He records it in the books of their deeds and will recompense them for it.

﴿So turn away from them﴾ (fa-a'riḍ 'anhum), and do not entertain in yourself any thought of vengeance against them. ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾ (wa-tawakkal 'alā Allāh) regarding their affair, for Allah will suffice you against their harm and will avenge you upon them when the affair of Islam grows strong. (p-378) ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs﴾ (wa-kafā billāhi wakīlā), meaning sufficient for whoever puts his trust in Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 82:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ That is: will they not contemplate its meanings (ma'ani) and its wording (mabani)? Tadabbur (reflection) is contemplation and looking into the backs (adbar) of matters, and into what they lead to in their final outcome; then it came to be used for every kind of contemplation. Tafakkur (reflective thinking) is the heart's turning over of proofs by considering them. This refutes the claim of some of the Rawafid (Rafidites) that the Qur'an's meaning cannot be understood except through the explanation of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the infallible Imam. It also indicates the validity of qiyas (analogical reasoning) and the invalidity of taqlid (blind imitation).

﴿And had it been from other than Allah﴾, as the disbelievers claimed, ﴿they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ That is: contradiction in respect of tawhid (affirming God's oneness), association (tashrik), permission (tahlil) and prohibition (tahrim). Or variation in respect of eloquence (balaghah): some of it reaching the limit of inimitability (i'jaz) while some of it falls short of that and could be matched. Or in respect of meanings: some of it being a report of an unseen matter that agreed with what it reported, and some of it being a report that contradicted what it reported; some of it indicating a sound meaning according to the scholars of ma'ani (the science of meanings), and some of it indicating a corrupt meaning that does not cohere. As for the heretics' clinging to verses in which they allege much discrepancy, such as His saying: ﴿so behold, it was a manifest serpent﴾ [al-A'raf: 107], ﴿as if it were a jinn﴾ [al-Naml: 10], ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 92], ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾ [al-Rahman: 39], the people of truth have already given answers to these, and you will find them explained in this book of ours in their proper places, God willing, the Exalted.

﴿When there comes to them a matter concerning security or fear﴾: these are some of the weaker Muslims who lacked experience of circumstances, or the hypocrites, who, whenever news reached them of the expeditions (sariyyah) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), whether of security and safety, or of fear and disorder,

﴿they spread it abroad﴾: they disseminated it. Their spreading it was corrupting. One says: "adhāʿa al-sirra" and "adhāʿa bihi" (he made the secret public). The pronoun refers to the matter, or to the security, or to the fear, because "aw" (or) requires one of them. ﴿And if they had referred it﴾: that news,

﴿to the Messenger﴾: the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ﴿and to those in authority among them﴾: meaning the senior Companions who were discerning in affairs, or those who were appointed to command from among them. ﴿would have known it﴾ (p-٣٧٩) : they would have known the plan behind what they had reported, ﴿those of them who deduce it﴾: who extract its plan by their acuity, their experience, and their knowledge of the affairs and stratagems of war. It was said: they would stand before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and those in authority, feeling secure and confident of victory over some of the enemies, or feeling fear and apprehension, and so they would spread it, and it would be publicized and reach the enemies, so that their spreading of it became corrupting. Yet if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority, and entrusted it to them, and acted as if they had not heard it, then those who deduce its plan (istinbat, drawing out rulings or conclusions by inference) would have known how they should manage it and what they should do or refrain from doing in it. The word "nabṭ" is the water that emerges from a well when it is first dug, and "istinbāṭ" is its extraction. It was then used figuratively for what a man extracts by the excellence of his mind of meanings and plans concerning what is difficult.

﴿Had it not been for the grace of God upon you﴾: by sending the Messenger, ﴿and His mercy﴾: by sending down the Book, ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾: you would have remained in disbelief, ﴿except for a few﴾: who did not follow him, but believed by reason, such as Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Qiss ibn Sāʿida, and others.

When God mentioned in the verses before it their holding back from fighting, their displaying obedience while concealing its opposite, He said: ﴿So fight in the way of God﴾, even if they leave you alone and forsake you, all by yourself.

﴿You are not burdened except with yourself﴾: other than yourself alone, in that you advance it to jihad. For God, the Exalted, is your helper, not the troops. It was said that he (ﷺ) called the people to go out at Badr al-Sughra (the Lesser Badr), and Abu Sufyan had arranged with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) the meeting there. Some people disliked going out, so this was revealed. He went out with only seventy men. Had no one followed him, he would have gone out alone.

﴿And urge the believers﴾: there is nothing upon you regarding their affair except urging them to fight, only that, not rebuking them.

﴿It may be that God will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾: i.e., their violence and ferocity, and they are Quraysh. God restrained their might through terror, so they did not go out. ʿAsā (perhaps, "it may be") is a word that raises hope, but raising the hopes of a generous person is more enduring than fulfilling the promise of a base one.

﴿And God is stronger in might﴾ than Quraysh, ﴿and stronger in punishment﴾: in torment. This is a tamyiz (a specifying accusative clarifying the noun), like "might" (ba'san) above.

(p-380)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 85:

﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession﴾: it is intercession for averting an evil or bringing about a benefit, while it is permissible under the Sharia.

﴿He will have a share of it﴾: a share of the reward of the intercession. ﴿And whoever intercedes with an evil intercession﴾: it is the opposite of the good intercession. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "No one is its interpreter other than me. Its meaning is: whoever commands monotheism and fights the people of disbelief, while its opposite is the evil intercession." Al-Hasan said: it is walking about to bring about reconciliation, and its opposite is slander (namimah).

﴿He will have a portion of it﴾: a share. ﴿And Allah is ever Muqit over all things﴾: Muqit means capable (muqtadir), from aqata ʿala al-shay': he had power over it; or it means Hafiz (Guardian, Preserver), from al-qut (sustenance), because it holds the soul and preserves it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 86:

﴿When you are greeted﴾, i.e., when someone greets you with peace (sullima ʿalaykum), for in our religion the greeting (tahiyya) is with peace in both abodes. ﴿Then greet with a better greeting than it, or return it﴾ [al-Nur 24:61]: ﴿So greet one another with a greeting from Allah﴾ [al-Nur 24:61]; ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:44]. The Arabs used to say at meeting: "Hayyaka Allah," i.e., "May Allah prolong your life." After Islam this was replaced by "al-salam" (peace).

﴿With a greeting﴾: it is on the pattern taf'ila, from hayya yuhayyi tahiyya. ﴿Then greet with a better greeting than it﴾, i.e., say: "wa ʿalaykumu al-salam wa rahmatu Allah" when he says "al-salam ʿalaykum," and add "wa barakatuh" when he says "wa rahmatu Allah." It is said: everything has an end, and the end of the salam is "wa barakatuh."

﴿Or return it﴾, i.e., respond to it with its equal. Returning the greeting is answering it with its like, because the one who answers repeats the words of the one who greets. There is an elided noun here, i.e., "return its like." Greeting is a sunna, and returning it is an obligation (fariḍa), while the better response is a virtue (fadl). There is no man who passes by a group of Muslims, greets them, and they do not return his greeting, except that the Holy Spirit (rawḥ al-qudus) is taken away from them, and the angels return it to him. Greetings are not returned during the khutba, during audible recitation of the Qur'an, during the narration of hadith, during the discussion of knowledge, during the adhan, and during the iqama. According to Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him: one does not greet the chess player or the backgammon player, the singer, the one who relieves himself, the pigeon-flyer, or the one who is naked without excuse in a bathhouse or elsewhere. A man greets when he enters upon his wife, the one walking greets the one sitting, the rider greets the walker, the rider of a horse greets the rider of a donkey, the young greets the old, and the fewer greets the more, and when they meet, they both begin (simultaneously). It is said: ﴿with a better greeting than it﴾ is for the people of the religion (ahl al-milla), and ﴿or return it﴾ is for the people of the dhimma. From the Prophet ﷺ: "When the People of the Book greet you, say: wa ʿalaykum." That is: "and upon you what you have said," because they used to say: "al-sam ʿalaykum" (death upon you). And his saying ﷺ: "There is no ghirar in greeting" means: one should not say "ʿalayka" (to one person) but "ʿalaykum," because his two recording angels are with him.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever over all things a Reckoner﴾, i.e., He will call you to account for everything in greeting and other than it.

**Allah** (the subject, mubtada') **there is no god but He** is the predicate (khabar), or else it is a parenthetical insertion (i'tirad). The predicate is **"He will surely gather you"**. Its meaning is: Allah, by Allah, He will surely gather you.

**"Until the Day of Resurrection"** means: He will surely assemble you to Him. **Al-qiyamah** (the Resurrection) derives from **al-qiyam** (standing), like **al-tilabah** and **al-tilab** (seeking, and what is sought). It is their standing up from the graves, or their standing for the reckoning: **"the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds"** (al-Mutaffifin 6). **"There is no doubt about it"** is a circumstantial clause (hal) of "the Day of Resurrection," and the pronoun (ha') refers to the Day. Alternatively, it is an attribute of a deleted verbal noun (masdar), meaning "a gathering about which there is no doubt," and the pronoun then refers to the gathering.

**"And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?"** The word **hadithan** (in statement) is a specification (tamyiz).
