The question is in the form of interrogation but carries the meaning of negation: no one is more truthful than Him in His report, His promise, or His threat, because lying is impossible for Him, since lying is ugly, being a report about a thing contrary to what it actually is.

﴿Fa-mā lakum﴾ (So what is [wrong] with you?) is a *mubtada'* (subject, the grammatical "topic") and *khabar* (predicate, the "comment") [of the sentence]. ﴿fī al-munāfiqīna fi'atayn﴾ means: What is [the matter] with you that you have disagreed about a people who have openly practiced hypocrisy (*nifāq*), and that you have split into two groups concerning them? And what is the matter with you that you have not definitively declared them to be unbelievers? The reason was that some of the hypocrites asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to go out to the desert (*al-badw*), claiming that they were ill from the unhealthiness of Madinah (*ijtiwā' al-Madīnah*). When they left, they kept travelling stage by stage until they joined the polytheists. The Muslims then disagreed about them: some said, "They are unbelievers," and some said, "They are Muslims." *Fi'atayn* is a *hāl* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject), like your saying: *Mā laka qā'iman?* (What is [the matter] with you standing?). Sibawayh said: When you say *mā laka qā'iman?*, its meaning is: "Why did you stand?" Its accusative case is [explained] by the interpretation: "What state can be firm for you in this condition?!"

﴿wa-Allāhu arkasahum﴾ (and Allah has overturned them) means: He returned them to the judgment of the unbelievers, ﴿bi-mā kasabū﴾ (because of what they earned), namely their apostasy and their joining of the polytheists. So [you should] return them [to unbelief] as well, and do not disagree about their unbelief.

﴿A-turīdūna an tahdū﴾ (Do you want to guide) means: to make them among those who are guided. ﴿man aḍalla Allāh﴾ (whom Allah has led astray) means: those whom Allah has made astray. Or [it means]: Do you want to call them "guided", when Allah has made their error manifest? In that case it is a rebuke to whoever named them "guided." The verse indicates our school's position on affirming *kasb* (acquisition, the human agent's earning of an act) for the servant, and creation (*khalq*) for the Lord, may His power be exalted.

﴿Wa-man yuḍlili Allāhu falan tajida lahu sabīlā﴾ (And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a path) means: a way to guidance.

[p-382]

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 89:

﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved﴾ The kaf (ka, "as") is an adjective (na't) of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), and ma is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), meaning: they wish that you would disbelieve with a disbelief like their disbelief.

﴿So that you would be alike﴾ is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon "you would disbelieve," meaning: you and they would be equal (mustawun) in disbelief.

﴿Sawa'an (alike)﴾ means: you and they being equal in disbelief.

﴿So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾: do not befriend them until they believe, because emigration in the way of Allah is by Islam.

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿then seize them and kill them wherever you find them﴾, as was the ruling for all polytheists.

﴿And do not take from among them an ally or a helper﴾: even if they offer you friendship and support, do not accept it from them.

ﷺ rendered as (ﷺ).

"Except those who reach a people between whom and you there is a covenant" — that is, who arrive at them and join them. The exception is from His words: ﴿So seize them and kill them﴾, [namely], without taking them as allies. The people here are the Aslam tribe. There was a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this was because he (ﷺ), before his departure to Makkah, had made a truce with Hilal ibn Uwaymir al-Aslami on the condition that he would neither assist him nor be assisted against him, and that whoever reached Hilal and sought refuge with him would have the same protection as Hilal had. The meaning is: kill them, except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant.

"Or who come to you" is a conjunction with the attribute of "a people": that is, except those who reach a people who are under treaty, or a people who hold back from fighting, neither with you nor against you. Or it is a conjunction with the relative clause "those who", meaning: except those who join those under treaty, or those who do not fight you.

﴿Their hearts are constricted﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) with qad implied before it. Al-ḥaṣr means constriction and contraction.

﴿from fighting you﴾: "from" (ʿan) means from fighting you, that is, from your fighting.

﴿Or fighting their own people﴾ alongside you.

﴿And had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you﴾ by strengthening their hearts and removing the constriction from them.

﴿So they would have fought you﴾ is a conjunction with "He would have given them power", and the entry of the lām is for emphasis.

﴿So if they keep away from you﴾, that is, if they do not confront you, ﴿and do not fight you, and offer you peace﴾, that is, submission and surrender,

﴿then Allah has not made for you any way against them﴾, that is, any path to fighting.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 91:

﴿You will find others who wish to be safe from you﴾ through hypocrisy, ﴿and to be safe from their own people﴾ through conformity. They are a people from Asad and Ghatafan. Whenever they came to Madinah, they professed Islam and made a covenant so that they would be safe from the Muslims. But whenever they returned to their people, they disbelieved and broke their covenants.

﴿Whenever they are returned to strife﴾ whenever their people call them to fight the Muslims.

﴿they are plunged into it﴾ they are overturned into it in the most vile and hideous manner; they were worse in it than any enemy. ﴿So if they do not withdraw from you﴾ so if they do not withdraw from fighting you,

﴿and offer you peace﴾ this is coordinated (ʿatf) with "do not withdraw from you," meaning: and they do not submit to you by seeking reconciliation, ﴿and withhold their hands﴾ this is also coordinated with it, meaning: and they do not refrain from fighting you.

﴿Then seize them and kill them wherever you find them﴾ wherever you have power over them and gain the upper hand against them.

﴿And for these We have given you a clear authority﴾ a manifest proof, because of the evident nature of their enmity, the exposure of their condition in disbelief and treachery, and their harm to the Muslims; or a clear dominion, since We have permitted you to kill them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 92:

﴿It is not for a believer﴾ (wa-ma kana li-mu'minin): it is not proper for him, nor fitting, nor suitable to his condition.

﴿to kill a believer﴾ (an yaqtula mu'minan) initially, without retaliation (qisas). That is, the believer is not like the unbeliever whose blood was previously declared permissible to shed.

﴿except by mistake﴾ (illa khata'an): except in the manner of error. This is an exceptive clause that is disconnected (istithna' munqati', disjunct exception) in the sense of "but" (lakin), meaning: but if a mistake occurs. It is also possible that it is a qualifier of the verbal noun (masdar), meaning: except a killing by mistake. The meaning is: it is not in the nature of a believer that the killing of a believer initially should ever exist in him, except when a mistake proceeds from him without intention, such as when he shoots at an unbeliever and hits a Muslim, or shoots at a person thinking he is an unbeliever, and then he turns out to be a Muslim.

﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake﴾ (wa-man qatala mu'minan khata'an): an adjectival qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, a killing by mistake.

﴿then the freeing of a slave﴾ (fa-tahrir raqabatin): the subject (mubtada') with an omitted predicate (khabar), that is, upon him is the freeing of a slave. Tahrir means manumission (i'taq). The free (hurr) and the noble (ʿatiq) mean the generous, because nobility belongs to free people just as baseness belongs to slaves; from this comes ʿitaq al-tayr (noble birds) and ʿitaq al-khayl (noble horses) for their excellence. Raqaba means a soul (nasama), and it is expressed by "head" in their saying: "So-and-so owns such-and-such a head of slaves."

﴿a believing [slave]﴾ (mu'minatin): It has been said: since he removed a believing soul from among the living, it became necessary for him to bring into the category of the free another soul like it, because releasing it from the bond of slavery is like giving it life, since the slave is reckoned among the dead, for slavery is one of the consequences of unbelief, and unbelief is death in legal terms.

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life…﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. Therefore he was prohibited from the dealings of free persons. This is problematic, for if it were so, it would also be required in the case of deliberate killing. But it may be said: this obligation was imposed on him because God the Exalted left the killer a believing soul, in that He did not impose retaliation, so He imposed upon him a believing slave in its place.

﴿and a blood-money paid to his family﴾ (diyatun musallamatun ila ahlihi): to be delivered to his heirs, who divide it just as they divide the inheritance; there is no difference between it and the rest of the estate in any respect, so the debt is paid from it, and the bequest is carried out. If there is no heir, it goes to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave the wife of Ashyam al-Dababi a share of the blood-money (ʿaql) of her husband Ashyam, but the blood-money is borne by the ʿaqila (paternal kin), while the expiation (kaffara) falls on the killer.

﴿unless they remit it﴾ (illa an yassaddaqu): unless they give it as charity to him, that is, they pardon him. The implication is: upon him is blood-money in every case, except when it is given to him as charity.

﴿But if he is from a people hostile to you﴾ (fa-in kana min qawmin ʿaduwwin lakum): if the one killed by mistake was from enemy people, that is, unbelievers, since "enemy" applies to all of them.

﴿and he is a believer﴾ (wa-huwa mu'min): that is, the one killed is a believer.

﴿then the freeing of a believing slave﴾ (fa-tahrir raqabatin mu'minatin): meaning: if a person of the enemy territory (harbi) embraced Islam in the abode of war and did not emigrate to us, and a Muslim killed him by mistake, expiation becomes obligatory for killing him, due to the protection that is conditioned by faith (al-ʿisma al-mu'thima), which is Islam; but blood-money is not obligatory, because the protection that gives value (al-ʿisma al-muqawwima) is tied to the territory, and it did not exist.

﴿And if he is from a people between you﴾ (wa-in kana): that is, the one killed,

﴿and between them there is a covenant﴾ (min qawmin baynakum): between the Muslims. Mithaq means a pact (ʿahd). ﴿then a blood-money paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave﴾: that is, even if the one killed is a dhimmi, his ruling is the ruling of a Muslim. This is evidence that the blood-money of a dhimmi is like the blood-money of a Muslim, which is our position.

﴿And whoever does not find﴾ (fa-man lam yajid) a slave: that is, does not own one, nor anything by which he can obtain one.

﴿then fasting for two months﴾ (fa-siyamu shahrayni): upon him is fasting for two months ﴿consecutively﴾ (mutatabiʿayni) ﴿as a repentance from God﴾ (tawbatan min Allah): an acceptance from God and a mercy from Him; "whoever God turns to" means when He accepts his repentance. That is, He has prescribed it as a repentance from Himself, or "let him repent in repentance," so it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar).

﴿And God is ever Knowing﴾ (kana Allahu ʿalimān) of what He commands, ﴿Wise﴾ (hakiman) in what He decrees.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 93:

﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun of the killer, meaning: intending to kill him because of his faith, which is disbelief (kufr); or killing him while considering his killing lawful (mustaḥill), which is also disbelief.

﴿Then his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ meaning: if He requites him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is his recompense if He requites him." Abiding (khulūd) may be intended to mean a long stay. The statement of the Mu'tazilah that one leaves faith (al-khurūj min al-īmān) contradicts the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178]. ﴿And Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him﴾ meaning: He has taken vengeance upon him and expelled him from His mercy. ﴿And has prepared for him a great punishment﴾ because of his committing a grave matter and a monstrous offense. In a ḥadīth: "The disappearance of this world is less significant to Allah than the killing of a Muslim man."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 94:

﴿O you who believe, when you go forth (ḍarabtum) in the way of Allah﴾ — that is, when you set out on the path of military campaign (al-ghazw). (p-386) ﴿Then investigate carefully (fa-tabayyanū)﴾ — Ḥamzah and ʿAlī read it as (fa-tathabbatū). Both are from the tafaʿʿul form with the meaning of istifʿāl (seeking), i.e., seek clarification of the matter and its certainty, and do not waver in it.

﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace (al-salām)﴾ — (al-silm) is read by Madanī, Shāmī and Ḥamzah. Both mean submission (al-istislām); it is said that it means Islam; and it is said that it means the greeting (al-taslīm) which is the salutation of the people of Islam.

﴿You are not a believer﴾ — this is in the accusative position as the object of "say." It is narrated that Mirdās ibn Nahīk embraced Islam, and none of his people embraced Islam except him. A detachment (sariyyah) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ attacked them, and they fled, but Mirdās remained, relying on his Islam. When he saw the horses, he drove his sheep to a winding place in the mountain and climbed up. When they caught up with him and shouted "Allahu akbar," he shouted too, and came down and said: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you." Usāmah ibn Zayd killed him and seized his sheep. They informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was greatly grieved and said: "You killed him only to seize what he had?!" Then he recited the verse to Usāmah.

﴿You seek the goods of worldly life﴾ — you seek the spoils, which are a perishable booty that quickly vanishes. It is this that calls you to abandon investigation and to neglect searching into the condition of the one you kill. (al-ʿaraḍ) means wealth; it was so named because of the swiftness of its passing away. (tabtaghūn) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject pronoun in (taqūlū).

﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾ — He will grant you booty, making you independent of killing a man who displays Islam and seeks refuge in it from being attacked in order that you may take his property.

﴿Thus you were before﴾ — at the first time you entered Islam, the word of testimony was heard from your mouths, and it protected your blood and property without waiting to ascertain the agreement of your hearts with your tongues. The kāf in (kadhālika) is the predicate of (kāna), and it has been placed before it and its subject.

﴿Then Allah conferred favor upon you﴾ — through steadfastness and being known for faith. So treat those entering Islam as you were treated.

﴿Therefore investigate carefully﴾ — the command to investigate is repeated to emphasize it upon them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ — so do not rush headlong into killing, but be cautious and careful in this matter.

(p-387)

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 95:**

﴿Those who sit at home﴾ from jihad, ﴿among the believers, other than those with a harm,﴾ is read with the accusative (*naṣb*) by Madani, Shami and ʿAlī, because it is an exception (*istithnāʾ*) from *al-qāʿidīn* (those who sit), or a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*) from them. It is read with the genitive (*jarr*) by Ḥamzah, as an attribute (*ṣifah*) of *al-muʾminīn* (the believers). It is read with the nominative (*rafʿ*), *ghayruhum* (other than them), as an attribute of *al-qāʿidūn* (those who sit). *Ḍarar* (harm) means illness, or a bodily defect such as blindness, lameness, chronic disability, or the like.

﴿And those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their selves﴾ is coordinated (*ʿaṭf*) with *al-qāʿidūn*. He negated equality between the one who strives and the one who sits without an excuse, although this is already known, as a rebuke (*tawbīkh*) to the one who sits back from jihad and as an incitement (*taḥrīk*) to it. Its like is: ﴿Are those who know and those who do not know equal?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. This is an incitement to seek knowledge and a rebuke for contentment with ignorance.

﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit back by a degree.﴾ He mentioned this sentence as an explanation (*bayān*) of the first sentence, clarifying what was negated of equality between those who sit back and those who strive. It is as if it were said: "What is wrong with them that they are not equal?" and this was answered by it.

﴿Darajah⁠﴾ (a degree) is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*maṣdar*), since it stands in the position of the single occurrence (*marrah*) of preference. It is as if it were said: "He preferred them with a preference," like your saying: "He struck him with a whip." The accusative of ﴿wa-kullan⁠﴾ (and to each) means: and each group of those who sit and those who strive. It is in the accusative because it is the first object (*maf ʿūl awwal*) of His saying ﴿Allah has promised⁠﴾, and the second is ﴿al-ḥusnā⁠﴾ (the best reward), that is, the best recompense, which is Paradise, even though those who strive are preferred over those who sit by a degree.

﴿And Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit back﴾ without an excuse ﴿with a great reward.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 96:

﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy﴾. It is said: "a jran" (ajran, "a reward") is in the accusative by "faddala" (He preferred), because it carries the sense of "ajarahum ajran" (He rewarded them with a reward). "Darajat" (degrees), "maghfirah" (forgiveness) and "rahmah" (mercy) are a substitution (badal) for "ajran". Or "darajat" is in the accusative in the manner of "darajah" (a degree), as if it were said: "He preferred them with preferences," like your saying: "He struck him with whips," meaning "with blows." And "ajran 'azima" (a great reward) is in the state (hal) of the indefinite noun, which is "darajat", placed before it. "Maghfiratan wa rahmah" (forgiveness and mercy) are by supposing their verb, meaning: "and He forgave them and showed them mercy, forgiveness and mercy." The summary of this is: God, exalted is He, preferred those who strive (al-mujahidin) over those who sit (al-qa'idin) by one degree when they have an excuse, and over those who sit without an excuse by the command of the Prophet (ﷺ), by way of sufficiency with others, (p-388) "darajat," because jihad is a collective obligation (fard kifayah). ﴿And God is ever Forgiving﴾ by covering over the excuse, ﴿Merciful﴾ by granting abundant reward.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 97:

It was revealed concerning those who embraced Islam but did not emigrate (hijrah), at a time when emigration was obligatory, and who went out with the polytheists to Badr as apostates and were killed in a state of disbelief: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾. It is permissible for this (verb, tawaffahum) to be in the past tense according to the reading of one who reads (tawaffathhum), and in the present tense with the meaning "We take them in death," the second tā' having been deleted because two tā's came together. Al-tawaffi (the taking up of the soul) means seizing the spirit, and al-malā'ikah (the angels) means the Angel of Death and his assistants. ﴿Wronging themselves﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun of the object in tawaffahum, meaning: in a state of wronging themselves by disbelief and by abandoning emigration.

﴿They will say﴾, that is, the angels say to those who are taken in death: ﴿"In what were you?"﴾, that is, "In what matter of your religion were you?" Its meaning is rebuke, that they were not in anything of the religion.

﴿They say: "We were oppressed (mustaḍʿafīn) on the earth"﴾, meaning unable to emigrate, ﴿on the earth﴾, the land of Makkah, so they (the polytheists) drove us out against our will.

﴿The angels say﴾, that is, the angels rebuking them:

﴿"Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you might emigrate therein?"﴾ They meant that you were able to leave Makkah for some of the lands where you would not be prevented from displaying your religion, and from emigrating to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The accusative of "fa-tuhājirū" is in answer to the interrogative. ﴿"Those, their refuge is Hell, and evil is it as a destination"﴾: the predicate of "inna" is "fa-ulā'ika." The entry of the fā' is due to the indefiniteness in "alladhīna" which resembles a conditional; or [the predicate is] ﴿"they said: In what were you?"﴾, and the returning pronoun is omitted, meaning: they said to them. The verse indicates that whoever is unable to establish his religion properly in one land, and knows that he can establish it in another, becomes obligated to emigrate. And in a ḥadīth: « "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it be a span of land, Paradise becomes due for him, and he will be the companion of his father Ibrahim and his Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)." »

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 98:

﴿Except the oppressed men, women and children﴾ He excepted from the people of the threat (al-wa'id) the oppressed (al-mustad'afin), who ﴿are unable to devise a plan﴾ to escape from it, due to their poverty and weakness, ﴿nor are they guided to a way﴾, meaning they have no knowledge of the routes.

﴿Are unable﴾ (la yastati'un) is a qualifier (sifah) either of "the oppressed" (al-mustad'afin) or of "the men, the women, and the children." It is permissible for this to be so even though the clauses are indefinite (nakirat), because the described noun, although it has the definite article (harf al-ta'rif), is not a specific thing (shay' bi-'aynihi), like his saying:

"And indeed I pass by the base man who abuses me."

﴿Then those, perhaps Allah will pardon them.﴾ *ʿAsā* (عسى), although it is for raising hope, is from Allah obligatory, because when the Generous one raises hope, He fulfills it. ﴿And Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving﴾ toward His servants before He created them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 4, verse 100:

﴿Whoever emigrates in the way of God will find in the earth many a refuge and abundance.﴾ *Muhājiran* (emigrating) and *ṭarīqan* (a path). He *yurāghimu* (is at odds with, defies) his people by his conduct, meaning he separates from them in spite of their noses, i.e., despite their displeasure. *Al-raghm* (humiliation) is abasement and disgrace. Its origin is the adhesion of the nose to *al-raghām*, which is dust. It is said: *rāghamtu al-rajul* (I defied the man), when you part from him while he dislikes your parting, out of the humiliation that befalls him because of it.

﴿many a refuge and abundance﴾: in provision, or in the public manifestation of the religion, or in the breast (i.e., in peace of heart), because fear is replaced by security.

﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant﴾: *muhājiran* is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*) referring to the pronoun in *yakhruj* (leaves).

﴿to God and His Messenger﴾: to wherever God and His Messenger have commanded.

﴿then death overtakes him﴾: before reaching his destination of emigration. This is a conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) on *yakhruj* (leaves).

﴿then his reward has fallen upon God﴾: meaning the reward has become due to him by God's promise. This is an affirmation of the promise, for nothing is obligatory upon God toward any of His creatures.

﴿And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾. They said: every emigration (*hijrah*) undertaken to seek knowledge, or for pilgrimage, or for jihad, or to flee to a land where one increases in obedience, contentment, or asceticism, or to seek lawful provision, is an emigration to God and His Messenger, and if death overtakes him on his way, his reward has fallen upon God.

(p-390)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 101:

﴿And when you travel in the land﴾: you journeyed through it. Thus "ḍarb fil-arḍ" (striking through the land, i.e., travelling) is the same as safar (journey). ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾: no sin or hardship ﴿if you shorten﴾: in that you shorten ﴿the prayer﴾: from the number of its units (rak'ahs), so that you pray the four-unit prayer as two units. The apparent meaning of the verse requires that shortening (qasr) is a concession (rukhsah) during travel, and completing it is the standard ('azimah), as al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said, because "junāḥ" (blame) is used in a context of lightening and concession, not in a context of the standard. We say: shortening is a standard, not merely a concession, and it is not permissible to complete the prayer, due to the saying of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him: "The prayer of travel is two units, a complete prayer, not a shortened one, upon the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ." As for the verse, they had become accustomed to completing the prayer, so they were liable to think that there was a deficiency upon them in shortening, and He removed the blame from them in order to reassure their hearts about shortening and to make them content with it. ﴿If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you﴾: if you fear that the disbelievers will target you with killing, wounding, or capture. Fear is a condition for the permissibility of shortening according to the Khawarij, the apparent sense of the text; according to the majority it is not a condition, on the basis of what was narrated from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said to 'Umar: "What is the matter with us that we shorten while we are secure?" He said: "I wondered at what you wondered at, so I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about that, and he said: 'It is a charity which God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity.'" In it is evidence that completing the prayer in travel is not permissible, because giving charity with something that does not admit of transfer of ownership is a pure remission that does not admit of rejection; and even if the one giving charity is one whose obedience is not obligatory, like the guardian of retaliation when he pardons, then the one whose obedience is obligatory is more fitting. Also, their state at the time of the revelation of the verse was like that, so it was revealed in accordance with the situation, and it is like His saying: ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ [al-Nur: 33]. Its evidence is the reading of 'Abd Allah: (from the prayer that they tempt you), meaning: lest they tempt you. Moreover, the intended meaning of the verse is shortening of the conditions, which is to signal with the head while on the mount when afraid, or to lighten the recitation, bowing, prostration and glorification, as was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: ﴿Indeed the disbelievers are to you a manifest enemy﴾, so they guarded against them.

(p-391)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 102:

﴿And when you (O Muhammad) are among them⦆ among your companions, ﴿and you lead the prayer for them⦆, meaning you intend to establish the prayer with them. Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him, held to its apparent meaning and therefore did not consider the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf) to be valid after him, peace be upon him. But the two (Abu Hanifa and Muhammad) said: The imams are deputies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in every age, so the address to him includes every imam, like His saying, ﴿Take from their wealth a charity that purifies them⦆ [al-Tawba: 103]. Its evidence is the action of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, after him, peace and blessings be upon him.

﴿Let a group of them stand with you⦆: that is, divide them into two groups, and let one of them stand with you, and pray with them, while a group stands facing the enemy. ﴿And let them take their arms⦆: that is, those who are facing the enemy. This is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. And if the intended meaning is those who are praying, then they said: they should take up of the weapons what does not distract them from the prayer, such as a sword, a dagger, and the like.

﴿And when they have prostrated⦆: that is, they have completed their rak'a with two prostrations. Prostration is taken in its apparent meaning according to us, while according to Malik it means the prayer itself. ﴿Then let them be behind you⦆: that is, when this group that is with you has prayed one rak'a, they should withdraw to take their position facing the enemy.

﴿And let the other group come who have not prayed⦆: in the position of a raised attribute of "a group." ﴿And let them pray with you⦆: that is, let the group that is positioned facing the enemy come, and let them pray the second rak'a with you.

﴿And let them take their precaution⦆: that by which they guard against the enemy, such as a coat of mail and the like.

﴿And their arms⦆: plural of silah (weapon), which is that with which one fights. Taking up arms is a condition according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, while according to us it is recommended. The manner of the prayer of fear is well known.

﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent of your arms and your belongings⦆: that is, they desired to catch you unawares during your prayer ﴿and they would incline upon you in one attack⦆, that is, they would charge upon you with one assault. ﴿And there is no blame upon you if you have discomfort from rain or are ill to put down your arms⦆, in putting down ﴿your arms, but take your precaution⦆. He granted them concession to lay down the weapons if carrying them became burdensome for them, due to rain that soaks them or illness that weakens them, and He commanded them, along with that, to take precaution, lest they become negligent and the enemy fall upon them.

﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment⦆: He informed that He humiliates their enemy, so that their hearts may be strengthened, and so that they know that the command to take precaution is not because of an expectation that they will overcome them, but is rather an act of worship from Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 103:

﴿So when you have completed the prayer﴾ i.e., when you have finished it, ﴿remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾. That is: persist in the remembrance of Allah in all circumstances. Or, [the meaning is]: when you intend to perform the prayer, then pray standing if you are able to, sitting if you are unable to stand, and lying on your sides if you are unable to sit.

﴿And when you are secure﴾ i.e., you have settled, with the removal of fear, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, i.e., complete it with one group [of worshippers]. Or: when you have established it, then complete it and do not shorten it. Or: when you are secure in health, then complete the standing, the bowing, and the prostration.

﴿Indeed, the prayer has been prescribed upon the believers at fixed times﴾, i.e., written and bounded by known times.

Surah 4, verse 104 (Commentary of al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil)

﴿And do not weaken﴾ (wa-la tahinu): do not become feeble, and do not be slack.

﴿in pursuing the people﴾ (fi ibtigha' al-qawm): in seeking out the disbelievers for fighting, and confronting them with it. Then He imposed the proof upon them with His words: ﴿If you suffer pain, then indeed they suffer pain as you suffer pain, and you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾. That is: the pain they find from wounding and killing is not specific to you; rather it is shared between you and them, afflicting them as it afflicts you. Then they endure it, so why do you not endure with the same endurance as theirs?! Especially since you are more worthy of endurance than they are, because you hope from Allah for what they do not hope: the making of your religion victorious over all other religions, and the great reward in the Hereafter.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ (wa-kana Allahu 'aliman): of the pain the believers find, ﴿Wise﴾ (hakiman): in the management of their affairs.

It is narrated that Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, one of the Banu Ẓafar, stole a coat of mail from a neighbour of his named Qatada ibn al-Nu'man, [hiding it] in a bag of flour. The flour began to scatter through a hole in it. (p. 393) He hid the coat with Zayd ibn al-Samin, a man from the Jews. The coat of mail was searched for at Ṭu'ma's, but it was not found there. Ṭu'ma swore that he had not taken it and that he had no knowledge of it, so they left him alone and followed the trail of the flour until it led to the Jew's house, and they took it. [The Jew] said, "Ṭu'ma gave it to me." Some Jews testified on his behalf. The Banu Ẓafar said, "Come with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and they asked him to argue on behalf of their companion. They said, "If you do not do so, our companion will be destroyed and disgraced, and the Jew will be cleared." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was inclined to do so, and then [the verse] was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth﴾, that is, "[while you are] upheld in truth," ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, by what He has made you know and revealed to you. Al-Shaykh Abu Mansur, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "By what He has inspired you with, through considering its foundational principles which were sent down." In this there is evidence for the permissibility of ijtihad (independent legal reasoning) on his part.

﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, that is, on behalf of the treacherous ones, ﴿a disputant﴾, one who argues, that is: do not argue on behalf of the Jews for the sake of the Banu Ẓafar.
﴿And seek forgiveness from Allah﴾ for what you had intended (*hamamta bihi*), ﴿indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 107:

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ They betray themselves by disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient is made a betrayal by them against themselves, because the harm returns to them. What is meant by this is Ṭu'ma (Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq) and those of his people who aided him, while they knew that he was a thief. Or it is mentioned in the plural form so that it encompasses Ṭu'ma and everyone who commits betrayal of the same kind.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer, sinful﴾ It was said in the intensive form (khawwān, "habitual betrayer") because He, exalted is He, knows of Ṭu'ma that he is excessive in betrayal and in committing sins. It is narrated that Ṭu'ma fled to Makkah, apostatized, and dug through a wall in Makkah in order to steal from its people, and the wall fell upon him and killed him. It was also said: "When you catch a man in an evil deed, know that it has siblings." And it is narrated from ʿUmar (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) that he ordered the amputation of the hand of a thief, and the thief's mother came weeping and said, "This is the first theft he has committed, so pardon him." He said, "You have lied. Indeed Allah does not take His servant to account for the first time."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 108:

﴿They hide﴾ (yastakhfūn): they conceal themselves ﴿from the people﴾ out of shame before them and fear of their harm.

﴿Yet they do not hide from Allah﴾: they do not feel shame before Him, ﴿while He is with them﴾: He is aware of them and watches over them, nothing of their secret conduct being hidden from Him. This verse is sufficient as a rebuke to people for the little shame and fear of their Lord that they have, despite knowing that in His presence there is no concealment and no absence. ﴿When they plot﴾ (yubayyitūn): they devise, and its origin is that it occurs at night.

﴿That which He does not approve of in speech﴾: this was the scheming of Ṭu'mah, who planned to throw the armour into the house of Zayd so that it would be stolen from him, while he swore that he had not stolen it. This is evidence that speech is the meaning that subsists in the self (al-kalām al-nafsī), since He called the scheming "speech." ﴿And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do﴾: knowing with comprehensive knowledge.

Ha, you are these people: "Ha" is an interjection of alerting attention, attached to "antum" (you), and "ulaa'" (these), and both are a subject and predicate. "Jadaltum" (you argued, disputed) means "khasamtum" (you contended), and it is a clause explaining the occurrence of "ulaa'" as a predicate, like your saying to one of the generous: "You are Hatim, you give away your wealth." Or "ulaa'" is a relative pronoun in meaning, "alladhina" (those who), and "jadaltum" is its relative clause. The meaning is: suppose you contended ﴿on their behalf﴾ on behalf of Tu'ma and his people ﴿in the life of this world, but who will dispute with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection﴾ meaning, who will contend on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment? It was also read as "anhu" (on his behalf), meaning on behalf of Tu'ma.

﴿Or who will be a guardian over them﴾ a protector, and a defender against the might of Allah and His punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 110:

﴿Whoever does evil﴾, a sin short of shirk, ﴿or wrongs himself﴾ with shirk, or "evil" (sū') means something ugly whose harm extends to others, as Ṭu'ma did to Qatāda and the Jew.

﴿Or wrongs himself﴾ with what is confined to himself, such as a false oath, ﴿then seeks forgiveness from Allah﴾ asks Him for His forgiveness.

﴿He will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful﴾ toward him. This is an exhortation to Ṭu'ma to seek forgiveness and repent.

[Qur'an 4:111] "And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself." Because its burden falls upon himself. "And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise." So He does not punish anyone for a sin other than its doer.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 112:

﴿And whoever commits a sin﴾, a minor one, ﴿or an offence﴾, or a major one. Alternatively, the first is a sin between himself and his Lord, and the second is a sin involving wrongs against people (maẓālim al-ʿibād),

﴿then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, as Ṭuʿma threw it upon Zayd, ﴿then he has taken upon himself a calumny﴾, a great falsehood, ﴿and a manifest sin﴾, an evident wrong. This is because by committing a sin he is sinful, and by casting blame on an innocent person he is slanderous, so he combines both matters. And buhtān (calumny) is a falsehood that stuns the one about whom it is said, concerning which he has no knowledge.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 113:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ — i.e., His protection (ʿișma) and His kindness (luṭf) from disclosing to you their secret.

﴿A group of them would have resolved﴾ — from the Banu Zafar. Alternatively, the intended "group" is the Banu Zafar, and the pronoun in "minhum" (of them) refers to the people.

﴿to mislead you﴾ — away from judging by the truth and pursuing the path of justice, while they knew that the culprit was one of their own.

﴿But they do not mislead except themselves﴾ — because the burden of it falls upon them.

﴿And they cannot harm you in anything﴾ — because you only acted upon the apparent state of affairs, and it did not occur to you that the reality was contrary to that.

﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿and wisdom﴾ — the Sunnah — ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾ — of the matters of religion and the laws, or of hidden affairs and the inner secrets of hearts.

﴿And the grace of Allah upon you has been ever great﴾ — in what He taught you and the favours He bestowed upon you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 114:

﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk﴾ — that is, the secret talk (tanaji) of people.

﴿Except for one who enjoins charity﴾ — except the secret talk of one who enjoins. It is in the genitive case (majrur) and is a substitute (badal) for "kathir" (much) or for "najwahum" (their secret talk). Or it is in the accusative case (mansub) as an exception of disconnection (al-inqita', i.e., munqati' or discontinuous exception), with the meaning: "but whoever enjoins charity, in his secret talk there is good."

﴿Or kindness﴾ — that is, a loan (qard), or relieving one who is distressed (ighathat malhuf), or every good deed (kull jamil). Or the intended meaning of "charity" (sadaqah) is zakat (obligatory alms), and of "kindness" (ma'ruf) is voluntary giving (tatawwu').

﴿Or reconciliation between people﴾ — that is, mending of relations (islah dhat al-bayn).

﴿And whoever does that﴾ — the aforementioned — ﴿seeking the pleasure of God﴾ — seeking the good pleasure of God. He excludes from this one who does that for show (riya') or for seeking leadership (tara'us). It is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu). The difficulty is that He said, ﴿Except one who enjoins﴾ and then said, ﴿And whoever does that﴾. The answer is that He mentioned the enjoining of good in order to indicate by it the one who performs it, because when the one who enjoins it enters among the group of the good, the one who performs it is all the more included among them. Then He said, ﴿And whoever does that﴾, so He mentioned the doer and joined to him the promise of a great reward. Or the intended meaning is "and whoever enjoins that," so He expressed the enjoining by the verb (fi'l).

﴿Then We will give him a great reward﴾ — (yu'tihi) is recited by Abu 'Amr and Hamzah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 115:

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾ — that is, whoever contravenes the Messenger after the evidence has become plain and the right path has manifested itself.

﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ — that is, the way in which they are upon the true (ḥanīf) religion. This is evidence that consensus (ijmā‘) is a proof (ḥujjah) whose opposition is impermissible, just as opposing the Book and the Sunnah is impermissible. For God the Exalted combined following other than the way of the believers with opposing the Messenger in the conditional clause, and made its recompense a severe threat; therefore following them is obligatory, just as allegiance to the Messenger is.

﴿We will turn him over to what he has turned to﴾ — We will make him a governor over the error he has chosen, and leave him with what he has selected in this world.

﴿and We will burn him in Hell﴾ — in the Hereafter, ﴿and it is an evil destination﴾. It has been said: this was revealed concerning Ṭu‘mah and his apostasy.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 116:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills.﴾ Its tafsir has already passed in this surah. ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ From the right way.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 117:

﴿Instead of Him, they invoke only female deities﴾ ما يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللهِ (what they worship besides Allah). ﴿Only female deities﴾: the plural of unthā (female), and they are al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāh. There was no tribe among the tribes of the Arabs except that they had an idol they worshipped, which they called "the female of the so-and-so tribe." It was also said: they used to say about their idols, "They are the daughters of Allah."

﴿They invoke only Satan﴾ what they worship, ﴿a rebellious Satan﴾, because he is the one who incited them to worship the idols, so they obeyed him, and their obedience to him became worship. ﴿Marīd﴾ means one who has gone out of obedience, stripped of good, and from it comes al-amrad (the beardless youth).

﴿God cursed him, and he said: "I will surely take﴾ are two descriptions, meaning: a rebellious devil who combines the curse of God with this shameful statement.

﴿from among Your servants a portion ordained﴾: cut off and obligatory for me, out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine, and one for God.

﴿And I will surely lead them astray﴾ by calling them to error, by making it seem attractive to them, and by whispering to them. Had the leading astray been up to him, he would have led all of them astray. ﴿And I will surely arouse in them false desires﴾, and I will cast into their hearts the false wishes concerning: long life and the attainment of hopes.

﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle﴾. The *batk* (cutting off) means cutting, and the *tabtik* (intensive form) indicates multiplication and repetition. That is: I will impel them to cut the ears of the cattle. They used to slit the ears of a she-camel when she had given birth to five offspring and the fifth was a male, and they forbade themselves to benefit from her. ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of God﴾: by gouging out the eye of the protected (*hami*) camel and releasing it from riding; or by castration, which is permitted for beasts but forbidden for the children of Adam; or by tattooing; or by denying lineages and attributing them falsely; or by changing gray hair to black; or by declaring things forbidden and lawful; or by effeminacy; or by altering the *fitrah* (innate nature) of God, which is the religion of Islam, in accordance with His saying: ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of God﴾ [Al-Rum: 30]. ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of God﴾ and responds to what he calls him to, ﴿has certainly suffered a manifest loss﴾ in both worlds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 120:

﴿He promises them﴾: he whispers to them that there is no Paradise, no Fire, no resurrection, and no reckoning.

﴿and arouses in them desires﴾ for what they will not attain. ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾: it is that he shows them something whose reality is the opposite of what appears.

(p-398)
﴿Those, their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any escape.﴾ *Ma'dilan* (a place to turn aside to), and *mafarran* (a place to flee to).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 122:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ and do not follow Satan in the command to disbelieve, ﴿We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾. And al-Nakha'i recited (sa-yudkhiluhum) ["He will admit them", with the verb in the third person singular]. ﴿A promise of Allah in truth﴾: both are verbal nouns (masdar). The first is emphasizing itself (mu'akkid li-nafsihi), and the second is emphasizing something other than itself (mu'akkid li-ghayrihi).

﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ "Qilan" means "qawlan" (speech). This is an interrogative used in the sense of negation, meaning: no one is more truthful than Him. This is a third emphasis. The purpose of these emphases is to contrast the false promises of Satan to his companions with the true promise of Allah to His friends.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 123:

﴿Not by your wishful thinking﴾ The matter is not according to your desires and wishful thinking, O polytheists, that the idols will benefit you.

﴿Nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾ Nor is it according to the desires of the Jews and the Christians, when they said: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved ones﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18] ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80]. ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, meaning: from among the polytheists and the People of the Book, as is shown by His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides God, any protector or helper﴾. This is a warning to the disbelievers, because after it He said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 124:

﴿Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer﴾. Here, His saying ﴿while being a believer﴾ is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). The first "*min*" (مِن) in ﴿min al-ṣāliḥāt﴾ is *lil-tab'īḍ* (partitive, indicating "some of"), and the second "*min*" (مِن) in ﴿min dhakarin aw unthā﴾ is *li-bayān al-ibhām* (explanatory, clarifying the vagueness in "whoever does"). This contains an indication that deeds are not part of faith.

﴿Then those will enter Paradise﴾: (*yudkhalūna*, "they will be admitted") is read by Makki (Ibn Kathir), Abu 'Amr, and Abu Bakr.

﴿And they will not be wronged the least bit (naqīr)﴾. The *naqīr* is the measure of a *naqīr* (a small pit or speck), which is the little hollow on the back of a date stone. The pronoun in ﴿they will not be wronged﴾ refers to both the doers of evil and the doers of righteous deeds together. It is permissible for the mention of it with one of the two groups to be evidence of its mention with the other. His saying ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ and His saying ﴿whoever does righteous deeds﴾ come after the mention of the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, like His saying ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin encompasses him﴾ [al-Baqara: 81], and His saying ﴿but those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ comes right after His saying ﴿and they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ /

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 125:

﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah﴾: he sincerely devotes his self (nafs) to Allah and keeps it whole for Him, recognizing for it no lord and no object of worship besides Him.

﴿while he is a doer of good﴾: one who performs good deeds (hasanat), ﴿and follows the religion (millah) of Ibrahim, a hanif﴾: inclining away from the false religions. This (hanif) is a circumstantial state (hal) either of the one who follows or of Ibrahim.

﴿And Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend (khalil)﴾: The root meaning is al-mukhall, which is the one who is a friend to you (yukhalluka), i.e., who agrees with you in your qualities (khilal), or who enters into the inner parts of your dwelling (khilal manzilik), or who fills your gap (khalal) as he fills its gap. Thus khullah (intimate friendship) is a purity of affection that necessitates special closeness through the penetration of secrets. Mahabbah (love) is purer, because it derives from the core of the heart (habbat al-qalb). This clause is an interjected sentence (jumlah i'tiradiyyah) that has no place in the i'rab (grammatical analysis), like the saying of the poet:

"... and calamities are numerous"

Its benefit is to emphasize the obligation of following his religion and way, because whoever has attained such nearness to Allah that He took him as a khalil is worthy that his religion and way be followed. If you were to make it coordinated (ma'tufah) with the sentences before it, it would have no meaning. And in the hadith: "Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil because of his feeding people food, his spreading the greeting of peace, and his praying at night while people are asleep." It was said: it was revealed to him, "I have only taken you as a khalil because you love to give and not to receive." In another narration: "Because you give to people and do not ask them."

(p-400)

In His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is evidence that taking Abraham as a close friend (khalil) was due to the friend's need for Him, not due to God's need for him, since He is exalted above such a thing. ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾, that is, knowing.

﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women.﴾ That is, they ask you for an *ifta'* (a legal ruling) concerning women. *Ifta'* (issuing a ruling, meaning the clarification of what is ambiguous): ﴿Say, "God gives you a ruling concerning them, and [so does] what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women.﴾ That is: God gives you a ruling. The recited [matter] in the Book, meaning the Qur'an, concerns the meaning of the orphans, namely His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans﴾ [al-Nisa': 3]. This is like your saying: "Zayd impressed me, and his generosity [impressed me]." "*Wa ma yutla*" (and what is recited) is in the nominative position, by coordination with the pronoun in "*yuftikum*" (gives you a ruling), or with the wording "Allah." And "*fi yatama al-nisa'*" (concerning the orphan women) is the complement of "*yutla*," meaning: it is recited to you concerning their meaning. It is also permissible for "*fi yatama al-nisa'*" to be a substitute (*badal*) for "*fihinna*" (concerning them). The idafa (genitive construction) here carries the sense of *min* (of/from). ﴿Those to whom you do not give what was prescribed for them﴾ means the inheritance that was ordained for them. A man among them would take an orphan girl into his own care along with her property. If she was beautiful, he would marry her and consume the property; if she was plain, he would prevent her from marrying until she died, so that he could inherit from her. ﴿And you desire to marry them﴾ means: you desire to marry them for their beauty, or you refrain from marrying them because of their plainness.

﴿And the weak among the children﴾ means the orphans. It is in the genitive case, coordinated with "orphan women." In the pre-Islamic period they used to pass inheritance only to men who were capable of managing affairs, excluding children and women.

﴿And that you stand up for the orphans﴾ is in the genitive case like "the weak," with the meaning: He gives you a ruling concerning the orphan women and concerning the weak, and concerning your standing up [for them]; or it is in the accusative case with the meaning: and He commands you that you stand up [for them]. This is an address to the rulers (*a'imma*), that they should look after them and secure their rights for them.

﴿With justice﴾ means with fairness in their inheritance and their property. ﴿And whatever good you do﴾ is a conditional clause whose answer is: ﴿indeed God is ever Knowing of it,﴾ meaning: He will reward you for it.

(p-401)

﴿And if a woman fears ill-treatment (nushuz, a breach of marital duties) or indifference from her husband﴾ She expects it from him, because of the signs and indications of it that have appeared to her. Nushuz means that he turns away from her by withholding himself and his maintenance from her, or by harming her with insults or beating.

﴿Or indifference﴾ from her: he speaks with her and keeps her company less, because of old age, ugliness, some defect in her appearance or character, boredom, or his eye wandering toward another woman, or for some other reason. (﴿there is no blame on them both if they make peace between themselves﴾) This is the reading of the Kufans (yuṣliḥā). The others read (yaṣṣālaḥā), meaning yatasālaḥā, which is its original form. The taʾ was changed to ṣād and assimilated (idgham, the merging of one consonant into the next). ﴿Peace﴾ (ṣulḥan) is in the sense of the verbal noun of each of the two verbs. The meaning of peace (ṣulḥ) is that they reconcile on the basis that she willingly gives up her share (of the night, the qasm), or part of it, or that she gives him part of the dowry, or all of it, or the maintenance.

﴿And peace is better﴾ than separation, or than nushuz, or than enmity in every matter. Or ﴿peace is better﴾ than all goods, just as enmity is worse than all evils. This sentence is a parenthetical insertion (iʿtirāḍ), like His saying: ﴿And souls have been made present to stinginess﴾, meaning that stinginess has been made present to them, never absent from them and never separated from them, that is, they are naturally disposed to it. The meaning is that a woman hardly ever willingly gives up her share, and a man hardly ever willingly grants her her share when he has become averse to her, so each of them seeks what brings them comfort. (Uḥḍirat) takes two objects, and the first is (al-anfus, the souls). Then He urged them to oppose their natural inclination and follow the Law with His saying: ﴿And if you do good﴾ by remaining with your wives even though you dislike them and love others, and by being patient in this out of regard for the right of companionship, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ (tattaqū), by avoiding nushuz, indifference, what leads to harm, and enmity. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do﴾ of good and piety, ﴿Acquainted﴾ (khabīran), and He will reward you for it.

It is related that ʿUmar al-Khārijī (of the Khawārij), who was one of the ugliest of the children of Adam, had a wife who was one of the most beautiful of them. She looked at him and said: "Praise be to Allah that you and I are among the people of Paradise." He said: "How?" She said: "Because you were given a wife like me and you gave thanks, and I was given a husband like you and I was patient, and Paradise is promised to the grateful and the patient."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 129:

﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives﴾ You will never be able to achieve justice and equality between women, such that no inclination whatsoever occurs. The completeness of justice is that they are made equal in turn (qasm), in maintenance (nafaqah), in care (ta'ahhud), in looking (nazar), in attention (iqbal), in pleasant company (mumalahah), in cheerful conversation (mufakahah), and in other matters. It has also been said that its meaning is: that you be just in love (mahabbah). "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to divide his time among his wives and would be just, and he would say: 'This is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control.'" He meant love, because 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, was more beloved to him.

﴿And even if you are eager﴾ striving diligently to pursue that, ﴿then do not incline completely (kulla al-mayl)﴾ do not be entirely unjust towards the one who is disliked, so that you deprive her of her turn without her consent. That is to say: avoiding complete inclination is within the limit of what is feasible, so do not go to excess in it, even if you fall short in full justice. There is in this a kind of reproach. "Kulla" is put in the accusative as an adverbial object (masdar), because it has the ruling of the noun to which it is attached.

﴿So you leave her like one suspended﴾ and she is the one who is neither a married woman with a husband nor divorced. ﴿And if you set things right﴾ between them,

﴿and guard against wrongdoing﴾ injustice, ﴿then indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ He forgives you the inclination of your hearts, and has mercy on you so He does not punish you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 130:

﴿And if they separate﴾, i.e., if the spouses do not reconcile over anything, and they part by khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), or by his divorcing her, and his paying her dower and the maintenance of her 'iddah (waiting period).

﴿Allah will make each of them independent﴾, each one of them, ﴿from His abundance﴾, from His wealth; i.e., He will provide him with a better spouse than his spouse, and a more pleasant life than his life. ﴿And Allah is ever All-Encompassing﴾ in permitting marriage [again] ﴿Wise﴾ in permitting release (divorce). So al-sa'ah (abundance) means wealth and capability, and al-wasi' (the All-Encompassing) means the Rich, the Capable.

(p-403)

Then He showed His self-sufficiency and power by His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (by creation), and He is the one who owns His servants as slaves. ﴿And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture﴾ — "those who were given the Scripture" (alladhina utu al-kitab) is a generic noun (ism li-l-jins), so it encompasses the heavenly scriptures — ﴿before you﴾ (from the earlier nations). The phrase "from before you" (min qablikum) is connected either to "We enjoined" (wassayna) or to "were given" (utu).

﴿And [We have enjoined] you﴾ (wa-iyyakum) is a conjunction (atf) upon "those who were given" (alladhina utu). ﴿That fear Allah﴾ (an ittaqu Allah) means "that they fear Allah" (bi-an ittaqaw), or it may be the explanatory "an" (an al-mufassira), because enjoining (tawsiyah) has the sense of saying (qawl). The meaning is: this is an ancient charge which Allah has always enjoined upon His servants — and you are not singled out for it — because by taqwa they attain happiness in His presence.

﴿And if you disbelieve﴾ (wa-in takfuru) is a conjunction upon "fear" (ittaqu), because the meaning is: We commanded them and commanded you to have taqwa, and We said to them and to you: ﴿And if you disbelieve — then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need﴾ (ghaniyyan) from His creation and from their worship, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ (hamidan), deserving to be praised for the abundance of His blessings, even if no one praises Him. The repetition of His saying ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ affirms what makes taqwa obligatory: since all creation belongs to Him, and He is their Creator and Owner, it is fitting that He be obeyed by His creation and not disobeyed. In this is evidence that taqwa is the root of all good. His saying ﴿And if you disbelieve﴾ immediately after taqwa is evidence that what is meant is guarding oneself against shirk.

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs (wakīl)﴾. So take Him as your Disposer (wakīl), and do not rely upon anyone other than Him.

Then He warned them and showed His power by saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾ (yuhdhibkum), i.e., annihilate you, ﴿O people, and bring others﴾ (ya'ti bi-akharin), i.e., create other people in your place, or a different kind of creation other than mankind, ﴿and Allah is ever, over that, Competent﴾ (qadiran), i.e., possessing perfect power.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 134:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, like the warrior who wages jihad seeking booty through his jihad, ﴿then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾. So why would he seek one of them to the exclusion of the other? And what he seeks (p-404) is the lesser of the two. ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of statements, ﴿Seeing﴾ of deeds, and this is both a promise and a warning.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 135:**

﴿O you who believe, be persistent in upholding justice﴾, striving to establish justice so that you do not deviate. ﴿Witnesses﴾ is a predicate following another predicate. ﴿For Allah﴾, meaning: you establish your testimonies (*shahadat*, "testimony") seeking the face of Allah. ﴿Even if it be against yourselves﴾: even if the testimony is against yourselves. Testimony against oneself is acknowledgment (*iqrar*) against oneself, because it has the meaning of testimony against oneself by binding oneself to a right. This is because the claim (*da'wa*), the testimony (*shahada*) and the acknowledgment (*iqrar*) all share in reporting a right of one person upon another. However, the claim is a report of a right for oneself against another, the acknowledgment is a report for another against oneself, and the testimony is for another against another.

﴿Or parents and relatives﴾, meaning: even if the testimony is against your fathers, your mothers and your relatives.

﴿Whether he be rich﴾: the one testified against, ﴿or poor﴾: his poverty does not prevent testimony against him out of pity for him. ﴿Allah is more worthy of both﴾, that is, of the rich and the poor, meaning: more concerned for them and more merciful to them. The pronoun in *bihima* ("of both of them") is dual, though it should have been singular, because the meaning is: whichever of these two (the rich or the poor) it is. This refers back to what is indicated by His words ﴿rich or poor﴾, namely the category of the rich and the poor, as if it were said: Allah is more worthy of the two categories of rich and poor, that is, of the wealthy and the poor. ﴿So do not follow your desires﴾ in wishing ﴿to deviate﴾ from the truth, from *al-'udul* ("deviation"), or from disliking ﴿to act justly﴾ between people, from *al-'adl* ("justice"). ((*Wa-in talu*) with a single *waw* and a *damma* on the *lam*, read by Ibn 'Amir of Syria and Hamza, from *al-wilaya* ("governing, taking charge").)

﴿Or you turn away﴾, meaning: even if you are entrusted with establishing testimony, or you turn away from establishing it, or others besides you (do so). (*Talwu*) with two *waws* and a sukun on the *lam*, from *al-layy* ("twisting"), meaning: if you twist your tongues away from testimony to the truth or from judging with justice, or you turn away from testifying with what you possess and withhold it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, so He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 136:

﴿O you who have believed﴾ is an address to the Muslims. ﴿Believe﴾: remain firm in faith and persist in it. Or it is addressed to the People of the Book, because they believed in some of the Books and Messengers and disbelieved in others. Or it is addressed to the hypocrites (munafiqin), meaning: O you who have believed outwardly (nifaqan), believe sincerely (ikhlasan). ﴿In Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾, that is, the Qur'an,

﴿And the Book which He sent down before﴾, that is, the category of what was sent down upon the prophets before him of Books. What indicates this is His saying: ﴿and His Books﴾. (Nazzala) and (anzala) are read by Makki, Shami and Abu 'Amr as (nazzala) and (anzala) respectively. Others read both with the active voice (ba'd al-fa'il) [as in ʾanzala and nazzala with the verb in active form]. It was said: "He sent down (nazzala) upon His Messenger" and "He sent down (anzala) before," because the Qur'an was sent down in portions, gradually (munajjaman), over twenty years, unlike the Books before it. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His Books and His Messengers and the Last Day﴾, that is, whoever disbelieves in any of these, ﴿has certainly gone far astray﴾, because disbelief in part of them is disbelief in all of them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 137:

﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ in Musa (peace be upon him), ﴿then disbelieved﴾ when they worshipped the calf, ﴿then believed﴾ in Musa after his return, ﴿then disbelieved﴾ in Isa (peace be upon him), ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾ by their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a way﴾ to salvation, or to Paradise. Or they are the hypocrites, who believed outwardly and disbelieved secretly, time after time. The increase in disbelief from them is their persistence in it until death, which is supported by His saying:

Announce to the hypocrites (bashshir al-munafiqin): tell them. The word "bashshir" (give good news) is used in place of it sarcastically (tahakkuman) toward them: "that for them there is a painful punishment (adhaban aliman), meaning one that causes pain (mu'liman)."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 139:

﴿Alladhina﴾ is in the accusative case as a form of censure (nasb ʿala al-dhamm), or in the nominative case, with the meaning: "It is intended, those who..." or "They are the ones who..." ﴿take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?﴾ The hypocrites (al-munafiqun) used to take the disbelievers (al-kafarah) as allies, seeking from them protection (al-mani'ah) and support (al-nusrah), and they would say: "The affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) will not be completed." ﴿Indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾ and to whomever He grants honour, such as the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, as He said: ﴿But honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

406

(p-406) ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another discourse. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in Hell﴾

140. (And He has already sent down to you) With the letter nūn vowelled with a fatḥa (nazzala): ʿĀṣim. With a ḍamma (nazzala, passive): the others.

﴿in the Book﴾ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿that when you hear the signs of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another discourse﴾ until they begin speaking about something other than disbelief and mockery of the Qur'an. Khawḍ (engaging) means beginning (shurūʿ). The ʾan here is a lightened form of the heavy (thaqīla) ʾanna, meaning: that when you hear, i.e., it was sent down to you that the matter is such-and-such. The "shaʾn" (matter) is what the sentence conveys with its condition and its response. The ʾan together with what follows it occupies a place of raising (rafʿ) as the subject of nuzzila, or a place of putting (naṣb) as the object of nazzala. The ones about whom it was sent down in the Book are those revealed to them in Mecca in His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in mockery of Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in another discourse﴾ [al-Anʿām: 68]. This is because the polytheists used to engage in discussing the Qur'an in their gatherings and mock it, so the Muslims were forbidden to sit with them as long as they were engaged in it. The hypocrites in Medina used to do something similar to what the polytheists did in Mecca, so they were forbidden to sit with them, just as they had been forbidden to sit with the polytheists in Mecca. ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them﴾ meaning in sin, if you remain with them. It does not mean likeness in every respect, for the hypocrites' engaging in it is disbelief, while the staying of these (believers) with them is disobedience.

﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in Hell﴾ because of their gathering in disbelief and mockery.

﴿Alladhina﴾ is either a substitute (*badal*, apposition) for "those who take," or a qualifier (*sifa*) for "the hypocrites," or it is in the accusative of censure (*nasb ʿala al-dhamm*) concerning them. ﴿Who wait for you﴾ means they await for you whatever new fortune or misfortune will befall you. ﴿If a victory from Allah comes to you﴾ means help and spoils of war. ﴿They say: "Did we not stand with you?"﴾ meaning, supporting you, "so give us a share of the spoils." ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾: He called the Muslims' triumph a "victory" (*fath*) to magnify their status, because it is a great matter for which the gates of heaven are opened. He called the disbelievers' success a "share" (*nasib*) to belittle their portion, because it is a morsel of this world that they obtain. ﴿They say﴾ to the disbelievers: ﴿"Did we not gain mastery over you"﴾, meaning, did we not overpower you and gain the ability to kill you, but we spared you? *Al-istihwadh* is *al-istila'* (seizing control) and *al-ghalaba* (overpowering).

﴿And protect you from the believers﴾ means by discouraging them from you, by suggesting to them what weakened their hearts, so that they became reluctant to fight you, and we were lax in supporting them against you. So give us a share of what you have obtained. ﴿Allah will judge between you﴾, O believers and hypocrites, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, so He will admit the hypocrites to the Fire and the believers to the Garden. ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, by the evidence of the beginning of the verse. Thus it is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. Or it means proof (*hujja*). Thus it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

(p-407)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 142:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah﴾. That is: they do what a deceiver does, by displaying faith and concealing disbelief. The munafiq (hypocrite) is one who displays faith and conceals disbelief; or [the verse means] "the friends of Allah," who are the believers. He attributes their deception to Himself as an honour for them: ﴿and He is their Deceiver﴾. He does to them what the one who overcomes in deception does, in that He leaves them with their blood and property protected in this world, while preparing for them the lowest level of the Fire in the next. The khadi' (deceiver) is the active participle from khadא'tuhu (I deceived him), fa-khada'tuhu (so I deceived him), meaning when you overcome him, and you were more deceptive than him (akhda' minhu). It has also been said: He recompenses them for the recompense of their deception. ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand up lazily﴾, burdened and reluctant. As for negligence, a believer may be afflicted with it. Kusala (lazy) is the plural of kaslan, like sukara (drunk) is the plural of sakran. ﴿They show off to the people﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: they intend by their prayer to make a display and to seek a reputation. Mura'ah (showing off) is a form of mufa'alah from ru'yah (seeing), because the one who shows off makes them see his deed, and they see it as commendable. ﴿And they do not remember Allah except a little﴾, that is, they do not pray except a little, because they never pray except while hidden from the eyes of the people; or it means they do not remember Allah with glorification and declaration of His oneness except a rare and small remembrance. Al-Hasan said: If that little were for Allah the Exalted, it would be much.

"Mudhabdhabin" (wavering, vacillating) is in the accusative as a term of censure, meaning "wavering" (muraddadin), that is, Satan and their desires have made them waver between faith and disbelief, so they are hesitant between the two, bewildered. The real meaning of "mudhabdhab" is one who is pushed away from both sides, that is, he is repelled and does not settle on one side; however, the word dhabdhabah contains a repetition that the word dhabb does not have. ﴿Between that﴾, between disbelief and faith. ﴿Neither to these﴾, not attributed to these (the believers), so that they would be believers; ﴿nor to those﴾, nor attributed to those (the polytheists), so that they would be named polytheists. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾, a path to guidance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 144:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ A clear proof, by which He would punish you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 145:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾. That is: in the level that is at the bottom of Hell. The Fire has seven levels (darakat, sing. daraka, "degrees" or "tiers"). They are so named because they follow one another, are successive, and are placed one above another. The hypocrite is punished more severely than the disbeliever because he was secure from the sword in this world, so he deserved the lowest level in the Hereafter as a matching recompense (ta'dil). Also, he shares the disbelief of the disbeliever, and to his disbelief is added mockery of Islam and its people. As for (al-darak) with a sukun on the ra', it is the reading of the Kufans, except for al-A'sha. With a fatha on the ra', it is the reading of the others. Both are dialectal forms (lughatan). Al-Zajjaj mentioned that the preferred reading is with a fatha on the ra'. ﴿And you will not find for them any helper﴾, one who would protect them from the punishment.

(p-409)

Except those who repent [of hypocrisy], and amend [what they corrupted of their secrets and their conditions during the state of hypocrisy]. This is an exception from the pronoun in the genitive in "and you will not find for them any helper."

And they hold fast to Allah [i.e., they trust in Him and rely on Him, as the sincere believers do], and they make their religion sincerely for Allah [they seek by their obedience nothing but His countenance]. Those will be with the believers [meaning they are the companions of the believers and their comrades in both abodes], and Allah will give the believers a great reward [so they will share in it with them]. The letter yāʾ is omitted in the script here, following the pronunciation.

Then He asked, affirming that He does not punish the believing, grateful one, saying: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful﴾ to Allah ﴿and believe﴾ in Him. Here "ma" (what) is in the accusative, governed by "yafʿalu" (does): "what does He do with your punishment?"

Faith (al-iman) is recognition of the Benefactor, and gratitude (al-shukr) is acknowledgment of the blessing, while disbelief in the Benefactor and in the blessing is obstinacy. Therefore the disbeliever deserves punishment. He mentioned gratitude before faith because the intelligent person looks at the great blessing upon him in his creation and in his being exposed to benefits, and so he gives thanks in a general, undifferentiated way. When his reflection leads him to recognize the Benefactor, he believes in Him, and then he gives thanks in a detailed way. Thus gratitude precedes faith. ﴿And Allah is ever Appreciative﴾ — He rewards you for your gratitude, or accepts the little of deeds and gives the abundant of reward. ﴿Knowing﴾ — knowing of what you do.

God does not love the public mention of evil speech (﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech﴾). Nor does He love any other kind of it, but public utterance is the more foul. ﴿Except by one who has been wronged﴾: except the public utterance of the one who has been wronged. He exempted from the public utterance that Allah does not love the utterance of the wronged, which is that he supplicates against the wrongdoer and reminds him of the evil that is in him. It has also been said: the "public utterance of evil speech" is cursing and abuse, and ﴿except by one who has been wronged﴾ means that if he returns the same to him, there is no blame upon him. ﴿And whoever retaliates after being wronged﴾ ﴿and Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of the complaint of the wronged, ﴿Knowing﴾ of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer.

(p-410)
